articles.title: In 2020, Cooper Kupp paid $2.5 million sight unseen for a 4-acre Wilsonville, Oregon home; he added a 4,600 sq ft indoor training hall and sold it in 2024 for $3 million
articles.summary: Discover the unique journey of NFL star Cooper Kupp as he transforms a $2.5 million Oregon estate with an indoor training facility into a lucrative $3 million sale, highlighting family, luxury, and athletic dedication.
articles.body: An offseason for a professional athlete could be a luxury home they can retreat to, and that would not be unusual. But what’s unheard of is if it were also a training ground. Cooper Kupp, Los Angeles Rams wide receiver, brought this idea to life. In 2020, he bought a four-acre property in Wilsonville, Oregon, sight unseen, according to Realtor. By August 2024, it found new owners for $3 million, after $500,000 was trimmed from the asking price. Kupp had initially listed the four-acre estate in September 2023 for $3.5 million, per Robb Report.The sale brought one particular feature of the estate to the fore: a 4,600-square-foot indoor athletic facility, built inside what used to be a barn. Kupp had used the space during the off-season before the Rams won Super Bowl LVI. The property also included a main residence, accommodating five bedrooms, and a separate guest house. This gave the listing a mix of family accommodation and sporting space. Kupp’s decision to let go of the estate was tied to practicalities of family life. In its September 25, 2023 report, Robb Report said he and his wife had less time to travel to Oregon with their three children. The home was about 30 minutes from Portland. By the time the sale was reported in August 2024, the property had been on the market for 11 months.A pandemic project turned a barn into a football training facilityBecause it was a celebrity home, its interior facilities were a major selling point. Robb Report described a turf-lined field, retractable basketball hoops at both ends, lighting, speakers and two oversized bay doors. In his own words, Kupp recalled the work that went into building and described it as a special part of the property. He said to the newspaper: “So much blood, sweat and tears went in there.”Kupp had fitted out the 4,600 square feet space during the pandemic. He also told Forber in 2023 that he completed most of his off-season preparations there before the Rams’ Super Bowl season. He added that the family had taken care in equipping the barn as a performance space center and that he would miss the early morning sessions done there. The facility was not the only space set aside designated for exercise. The four-car garage had been arranged as a gym. The indoor field room was used for football drills, and the retractable hoops were used for basketball practice.According to the Realtor, the main house was built in 1997. The rooms included an office with a fireplace, a family room with a bar and wine fridge, and a formal dining room with coffered ceilings and chandeliers. Robb Report added that the exterior design was Gothic Revival, with hardwood floors, natural stone details, large windows and decorative woodwork, natural stone details, large windows and decorative woodwork.The house, its grounds, and the final sale The main residence had five bedrooms and 6.5 bathrooms. The kitchen had a large island and appliances by Miele and Sub-Zero, and later the former received updated appliances and hardware, along with paint, wallpaper, and stone finishes.The main bedroom had access to the rear grounds and an adjoining bathroom with a deep bath and glass shower. On the ground floor, the primary suite also had a private vestibule and its own patio. Upstairs, there were also four other bedrooms. The property also had a separate guest cottage. It included a bedroom, laundry room and covered patio. The estate sat on a little over four acres, about 17 miles south of Portland. Robb Report in 2023 had earlier described an almost 2,000-square-foot guest house.Kupp, who hails from Washington, played college football at Eastern Washington University before being selected by the Rams in the third round of the 2017 NFL Draft. He was named the Most Valuable Player of Super Bowl LVI, which the Rams won after the 2021 season.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: In 2023, Joe Burrow bought a 7,300-square-foot Ohio mansion; 3 years later, its private setting still sets it apart
articles.summary: Joe Burrow bought a 7,300-square-foot home in Anderson Township, Ohio, in July 2023 for $7.5 million.
articles.body: Joe Burrow bought a 7,300-square-foot home in Anderson Township, Ohio, in July 2023 for $7.5 million. The Bengals quarterback signed a five-year, $275 million extension two months later. The house sits on about three acres above the Ohio River and was the most expensive home sale in Hamilton County that year. Three years on, people still talk about it for one reason: it is hard to see from the road, and that matters more than the price.What makes Joe Burrow’s Ohio mansion so private?Start with the land. The estate sits on roughly three acres in the Coldstream area of Anderson Township, on what was reportedly once a horse farm. Reports differ on the details. Some say four bedrooms and six bathrooms, others say five and seven, and the build year is listed as 2014 in some places and 2016 in others. What every account agrees on is the setting: space, trees and views of the Ohio River.That space is the point. In a city with a lot of football fans, a home on a quiet, wooded lot gives a quarterback somewhere to switch off. Fans can find the neighborhood. Getting a clear look at the house is another matter.The area also fits the job. Reports put the home about 15 minutes from Paycor Stadium. At the time of purchase, Bengals teammates Joe Mixon and Orlando Brown Jr. were also living nearby, so Burrow was not isolated. He had company close by and distance from everyone else.Why Joe Burrow chose a quieter home after years in the cityJoe Burrow’s first Cincinnati home was a 2,900-square-foot house in Columbia Tusculum, bought in 2020 for $835,000. It suited a rookie. It was close to everything, and it was a long way from the kind of space a franchise quarterback eventually wants.The new place was a different kind of purchase. Reports said he bought it before the extension was signed, and that he moved in soon after, fully furnished. A few months later, a wrist injury against the Ravens in November 2023 ended his season. Rehab is slow, lonely work, and a quiet house with room to move probably helped.There was also a smart money angle. Burrow bought in July, before Hamilton County released its latest property tax assessments. The previous owner paid $70,679 in property taxes for 2023, while Burrow’s bill for 2024 came in at $56,294. It is a small detail, but it shows a quarterback who reads the field away from the field too.His roots are worth remembering. He grew up in Athens, Ohio, and his family home there was bought in 2005 for around $240,000. Staying in the state was never just a business decision for him.How the December 2024 break-in tested the estate’s privacyA long driveway and a wooded lot offer comfort, but they do not make a home secure. That became clear on Dec. 9, 2024, while Burrow was in Arlington, Texas, playing the Cowboys on Monday Night Football.Authorities were called to the house around 8:14 p.m. A window was shattered and the bedroom was ransacked. Investigators later said designer bags, watches, jewelry and other items worth nearly $300,000 were taken. According to the U.S. Attorney’s office, a trail camera caught a man carrying luggage through the woods behind the property. The same trees that give Burrow privacy gave the thieves cover.Burrow spoke about it afterward. “I understand it’s the life that we choose,” he said, adding that it does not make the experience any easier to deal with.Police made a break a month later. On Jan. 10, 2025, Ohio State Highway Patrol troopers stopped a vehicle in Clark County and arrested four Chilean men. Inside, they found burglary tools and an old LSU shirt and Bengals hat believed to be stolen from the Burrow home. All four were found to be in the country illegally. Three of them, Sergio Cabello, Jordan Sanchez and Bastian Morales, were later charged in federal court and in Hamilton County. They pleaded not guilty in federal court. Prosecutors also pointed to a photo in which the suspects wore Burrow’s “JB9” necklaces.The case was part of a wider pattern. The FBI warned pro athletes after a run of burglaries that also hit other stars, including Patrick Mahomes and Luka Doncic.What the Joe Burrow mansion says about living in the spotlightThe lesson is not that the house failed. A secluded estate did what it was meant to do for years, and the break-in happened when no one was home and a game was being watched by millions. Even so, privacy at this level is never only about trees and distance.Players now live in a world where schedules are public. When a team travels or plays on national television, everyone knows who is away. That is why security work has become as routine for athletes as film study. Reports from the night noted that an officer was already working security at the property when the break-in was reported, which shows how seriously the setup was taken.Burrow has kept living there since. For a quarterback who takes hits for a living, a home that feels like a place to breathe still matters. The price tag drew the headlines in 2023. Three years later, the more interesting story is how much a long driveway, a thick tree line and a view of the river can and cannot protect.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Jason Kelce's $680,000 home turned into a nearly $6 million Pennsylvania estate, but neighbours are raising serious concerns over his expansion plans
articles.summary: Jason Kelce's real estate journey in Pennsylvania began with a relatively modest purchase.
articles.body: Jason Kelce's real estate journey in Pennsylvania began with a relatively modest purchase. Today, the retired Philadelphia Eagles star has assembled a sprawling property compound worth nearly $6 million in combined purchase costs. What started as a four-bedroom home gradually became a much bigger family project, with neighbouring properties joining the estate over several years. However, expanding the land brought unexpected challenges. Plans for another house and a privacy fence eventually reached a local zoning board after neighbours raised concerns about construction, changing slopes and possible water runoff.Jason Kelce's $680,000 home became a nearly $6 million property investmentJason Kelce and Kylie Kelce began building their property portfolio in 2018, the same year they got married. Their first purchase was a four-bedroom home in Haverford, an upscale Philadelphia suburb. Jason paid $680,000 for the property, which reportedly had 2.5 bathrooms, a three-car garage, a greenhouse and an outdoor swimming pool with waterfalls and a hot tub.The house also had a finished basement with a fireplace. It later became familiar to fans because Jason used the space to record episodes of his popular New Heights podcast with his brother, Travis Kelce.However, the former Eagles centre had bigger plans for the surrounding land. In 2020, he purchased an adjoining eight-acre property for $3.96 million. Three years later, he added another neighbouring parcel for $1.35 million.The three purchases brought his total reported spending to approximately $5.99 million. Together, the properties created a compound covering roughly 10 acres.It is important to distinguish the combined purchase price from the estate's current market value. The nearly $6 million figure reflects what the Kelces reportedly paid for the properties, not a confirmed appraisal or recent sale.Jason Kelce's 10-acre Pennsylvania estate has bigger family plansThe growing property portfolio is closely connected to the couple's desire to establish a long-term family home in Pennsylvania. Jason Kelce and Kylie Kelce have remained in the Philadelphia area even after his retirement from professional football.Haverford also has a personal connection for Kylie, making the location more than a convenient address for the former NFL star. Rather than moving to a different city after his playing career, Jason has continued investing in the community where they started their married life.The family compound also offers room for privacy, recreation and work. The existing home has features that support family life, while the adjoining land gives the couple more freedom to plan a larger residence.By 2025, their plans had moved beyond purchasing additional land. The couple wanted to build another house on the estate, creating more space for their growing family. They also sought permission to change parts of the property and install additional fencing.Jason personally appeared before the Haverford Township Zoning Hearing Board on February 20, 2025, to explain the proposed changes.His appearance was notable because the former football star rarely needed to deal with the kind of local planning issues that come with expanding a large private estate. This time, however, he wanted officials and neighbours to understand why the changes mattered to his family.Jason Kelce's mansion expansion sparks neighbour concerns over floodingThe proposed construction did not receive an entirely smooth reception. Some neighbours questioned how the work could affect surrounding properties, particularly when it came to rainwater and drainage.One of the main concerns involved removing slopes from the land to prepare a relatively flat area for the planned house. Residents worried that changing the natural flow of water could increase runoff and create flooding problems during construction.Neighbour Wendy De La Rosa raised the issue during the zoning hearing. According to local reporting, she had already noticed changes to her property when it rained.Her concerns were not simply about the appearance of the estate or the construction activity. Water flowing onto neighbouring land could create problems for nearby families, especially if the work changed existing drainage patterns.The discussion became an important part of the hearing.Civil engineer Timothy Davis explained that the slopes were not entirely natural. They had been created decades earlier when a house was built on the land and an elevated section was formed to provide access to a swimming pool.He also addressed the concerns about construction and drainage, explaining that temporary runoff could increase while work continued. However, sediment controls had been put in place, and the team was prepared to direct water towards a more suitable location.The disagreement showed how even a multimillion-dollar property project can affect the wider neighbourhood. For the Kelces, the goal was to create a more private family residence. For nearby residents, protecting their own homes from possible water damage remained equally important.Jason Kelce explains why his family needs a privacy fenceWater management was not the only issue discussed at the hearing. The Kelces also wanted permission to install a fence that would improve security around their property.As Jason's public profile grew through his NFL career, media appearances and the success of New Heights, maintaining privacy became more difficult. His family also attracted attention because of his connection to Travis and the growing popularity of Kylie.Jason explained that the proposed fence was intended to reduce unnecessary foot traffic near their home without making the property look out of place in the neighbourhood.Speaking at the February hearing, he said:"We wanted to be in this area," Kelce said. "We like this area a lot."He also explained the family's security concerns, saying:"Obviously things for my family are quite unique with the security purposes. We’d like to just deter a little bit of the foot traffic coming in and out of the home, so we were trying to put a fence that sufficiently does that while also appeals to the aesthetic of the area and that people would appreciate."The proposal included changes to the existing driveway, a gated entrance and additional fencing. The design team also planned to retain parts of the existing fence and add landscaping to soften the appearance of the new sections.The intention was to balance security with the character of the surrounding street. The Kelces did not want the estate to feel completely disconnected from the community.Jason Kelce gets zoning approval, but his $5.99 million estate still has work aheadAfter hearing from the Kelces, their representatives and nearby residents, the zoning board approved the requested variances. However, the decision came with conditions designed to address the concerns raised during the meeting.The most important requirement involved stormwater management. The Kelces would have to ensure that runoff from their construction work did not adversely affect neighbouring properties. The board also required the approved work to be completed within two years.The decision allowed the family to move forward with their plans, but it also made clear that property expansion comes with responsibilities beyond the boundaries of private land.For Jason, the project represents another chapter in a career that has changed considerably since he retired from the NFL in 2024. His success with the Philadelphia Eagles helped establish him as one of the league's most recognisable centres. His media work and business ventures have since given him a new public platform.His Pennsylvania estate reflects that transition. What began as a $680,000 home has developed into a nearly $6 million property compound through three separate purchases.The expansion has brought new possibilities for the Kelce family, but it has also placed their plans under the scrutiny of the local community. And while the zoning approval cleared an important hurdle, the challenge now is to complete the project while keeping the neighbours' concerns in mind.For a family seeking more privacy, the nearly 10-acre estate may offer plenty of space. Making the ambitious expansion work for everyone around it is another matter.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Inside Tom Brady’s billionaire bunker plans: The Miami waterfront lot that put the seven-time champion next to some of the richest neighbors in America
articles.summary: Tom Brady paid $17 million for a teardown lot on Miami’s Indian Creek Island in late 2020.
articles.body: Tom Brady paid $17 million for a teardown lot on Miami’s Indian Creek Island in late 2020. Over the next few years he turned it into a finished waterfront estate. The island, nicknamed the Billionaire Bunker, is home to Jared Kushner, Ivanka Trump and Jeff Bezos. In January 2025, Bloomberg reported that bids on Brady’s house had passed $150 million, though no public listing followed. A sale at that level would beat Miami’s single-family record.How Tom Brady ended up on Miami’s Billionaire BunkerTom Brady was still a Tampa Bay Buccaneers quarterback when the deal came together. Page Six reported in December 2020 that he and then-wife Gisele Bündchen had bought the property at 26 Indian Creek Island Road. The couple were renting Derek Jeter’s Tampa mansion at the time, so the purchase was a quiet bet on life after football.The transaction appears to have happened off market. It went through an LLC tied to Jeff Soffer’s Fontainebleau Development. Soffer is a close friend of Brady and lives next door at number 27. That detail says a lot about how deals work on the island: introductions matter as much as price.The lot covers roughly two acres, with about 200 feet of water frontage, according to reports at the time. The plan from the start was to demolish the existing house and build something new and eco-friendly. Brady retired for good in February 2023, so he did not live there while he played. He bought the place for the years after the game.Why the island earned its bunker reputationIndian Creek is a man-made island in Biscayne Bay, and it works more like a private village than a neighborhood. It has an 18-hole golf course and a country club. It also has its own police force and its own mayor. Access is gated and tightly controlled.The neighbors explain the nickname. Kushner and Ivanka Trump reportedly paid more than $30 million for their lot. Billionaire investor Carl Icahn has a home there. Bezos has spent more than $230 million on three properties since 2023, according to Business Insider and Bloomberg.For someone with Brady’s profile, the appeal is easy to read. He spent twenty years being watched. On Indian Creek, the real product is privacy. The price tag mostly pays for the security around the house, not just the house itself.What Tom Brady built on the waterThe build was not cheap, and it was not quick. In 2023, The Real Deal reported that Brady had secured a $35 million construction loan for the property. First Republic Bank was the original lender, but it failed, and JPMorgan stepped in to provide the financing. That loan alone suggests the construction bill ran well into eight figures.Renderings from Scott Mitchell Studio, obtained by The Real Deal in September 2023, showed a modern waterfront house. The primary and guest suites each have their own terraces. Later reports described a pickleball court, a basketball court, a custom golf area, an outdoor infinity pool and a boat dock. The mansion was reported complete in 2024.The divorce changed the story around the house. Brady and Bündchen split in 2022, and per their settlement, Brady kept the Indian Creek property. Bündchen moved into her own place in Surfside, bought for $11.5 million. It sits almost directly across the water from his estate. Two homes that were once planned as one family’s future now look at each other across a short stretch of bay.Why $150 million bids are only part of the storyThe Bloomberg report in January 2025 said Brady was open to selling and that the house was being shown to a small group of buyers. Bids had reportedly topped $150 million. Bloomberg also noted that those discussions did not guarantee a sale, and Brady’s representatives did not comment.The number looks less strange against the island’s recent market. Ken Griffin set Miami’s previous single-family record in 2022, paying $107 million for a Coconut Grove estate. A vacant 1.84-acre lot on Indian Creek, bought for $27.5 million in 2018, was later on the market for $200 million. Bezos moving in lifted everything around him.Then the ceiling moved again. In March 2026, the Wall Street Journal reported that Mark Zuckerberg had bought an Indian Creek mansion for $170 million, now the largest residential sale in Miami-Dade County. That means a Brady sale at $150 million would no longer take the record. It would still land among the biggest deals the city has seen.For now, the facts are narrower than the headlines. Brady bought a $17 million lot, built a house on it and has been reported to have heard offers far above that. No public sale record has confirmed a deal. The most useful number may be the oldest one: $17 million was what the land cost in 2020, before Bezos, before Zuckerberg, and before the island became a bidding war.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Panthers corgi race goes awry after dog escapes, breaks multiple tackles before being caught
articles.summary: One corgi refused to go down in Week 9.
articles.body:
The biggest play from the Carolina Panthers vs. Denver Broncos game from Sunday may not have even come during the contest … and may not have involved an actual player.

Hijinks ensued after a corgi went rogue during a race at halftime. The corgi decided to break free from the actual race, and then took handlers on a comical route before the pooch was eventually wrangled.

The corgi broke roughly five or six tackles and pulled off a few jukes before the canine was finally taken down around the 40-yard line. Presumably, the dog was not hurt on the play.

The actual game was also exciting, with the Panthers and Broncos keeping things close well into the third quarter. Darren Waller and Chuba Hubbard each had big moments for Carolina and Courtland Sutton scored a touchdown for Denver.

It was, however, the corgi who stole the show.

That shouldn't necessarily come as a surprise. Compared to every other player who took the field Sunday, the corgi — as you might expect — had the most dog in him.

articles.title: "I was living off him": Travis Kelce opens up about how Jason Kelce stood by him through financial issues in his career

articles.body: Travis Kelce, the Kansas City Chiefs’ star player, and his older brother, Jason Kelce, have built a business empire of their own as their $200 million Ohio based Garage Beer has been highly profitable. While their bond with one another has been pretty inspiring, the tight end Travis Kelce has reflected on how Jason Kelce has helped him through financial and professional issues.Travis Kelce opens up on how Jason Kelce helped him through financial and professional issues as they build a business empireIn an interview with NBC News, the Kansas City chiefs’ tight end Travis Kelce opened up about it as he said, "When I got removed from the team I got my scholarship taken so I was staying with my brother, I was in his room and his house, kind of like two brothers growing up living in the same room…”The Kansas City Chiefs’ star tight end added, "So in terms of rent I wasn't paying rent, in terms of food he was helping me with food, so I was literally living off him for quite a while down there and he was my lifeline.”The 37 year old Super Bowl champion continued, “I was trying to do the right things, and he went into the coaches' office and talked to numerous coaches and numerous people in the Cincinnati staff to try to get me another chance to be on the team. When I say I owe it all to him, I really do."Travis Kelce’s college drug scandal became the lowest point of his life before he bounced backFor the unversed, the Kansas City Chiefs tight end Travis Kelce failed a drug test in 2-010 as he even ended up missing the Sugar Bowl that year after he was suspended.As per reports, the star player had smoked marijuana as he was even accused of violating team rules due to off field partying.In many of his interviews, the top tight end Travis Kelce has often spoken about the regrets he has had and how he even needed to go to a shrink back then to help him through his issues.For the Kelce family, it was one of the lowest points as Travis Kelce’s mother Donna Kelce has expressed how worried she was for her younger son.Despite the issues, Travis Kelce managed to join the Kansas City Chiefs in 2013 and life changed for him overnight.Today, Travis Kelce and Jason Kelce continue to work together as their podcast has been a huge hit among fans while their Garage Beer brand makes high profits.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Is Madison Beer to blame for Justin Herbert’s slump? Why the engagement, the celebrity spotlight and the winless Chargers have fans arguing before the Week 9 game against the Texans
articles.summary: The Chargers are 0-7, Justin Herbert is completing fewer passes than at any point in his career, and part of the fan base has picked a culprit: his
articles.body: The Chargers are 0-7, Justin Herbert is completing fewer passes than at any point in his career, and part of the fan base has picked a culprit: his fiancée, Madison Beer. Nothing in the reporting backs that up. The couple announced their engagement on a Tuesday in late July, and the slump has played out in public since September. Los Angeles hosts the Texans in Week 9 on Sunday, still looking for a first win. The numbers point to problems that have little to do with Herbert's personal life.The Madison Beer theory and where it came fromIt is easy to see why it caught on. Madison Beer's year has been loud. Her album Locket arrived in January, a tour followed, and in late September she was announced as a Fortnite Icon Series collaboration. Herbert, meanwhile, introduced her to the world as his fiancée. Put a busy celebrity calendar next to a winless team and some people will connect the dots. Athletes' partners have taken this kind of heat for decades, usually with nothing behind it but a bad month.The timeline does not hold up, though. The two started dating in August 2025, and Herbert's 2025 season was a good one. He finished just inside the top 10 among quarterbacks in pass attempts, yards and touchdowns, and set career highs in carries and rushing yards. If a relationship was going to hurt his play, it took a full year to show up.No one with the team has been reported pointing that way either. After the Rams loss, a reporter asked Jim Harbaugh whether he had considered benching Herbert. The coach answered with one word: "No." He added that most players in the locker room had never been in this spot before.What Justin Herbert's numbers say about the slump?The Week 8 line is a decent snapshot. Herbert went 24 of 32 for 257 yards in a 24-9 loss to the Rams, with no touchdowns, two interceptions and a lost fumble to his name. Through seven games he has a 5:10 touchdown to interception ratio and a 61.8 percent completion rate, a career low by a wide margin. He leads the league with 10 turnovers and has gone eight straight starts, playoffs included, without multiple total touchdowns.That run started before this season. A slump that long says something about the whole offense, and it puts coordinator Mike McDaniel in the frame. The Chargers declined to move on from him during the bye week. Even Herbert's best passing day of the year, a 75 percent completion rate, ended with two picks.The outside noise keeps growing. Hall of Famer Cris Carter wants the Chargers to trade Herbert while his value is still high. ESPN's Adam Schefter said the team would not consider it.Sunday gives Houston a look at a quarterback who has not thrown a touchdown pass in two straight games. If Herbert plays clean, the Beer talk will fade fast. If he does not, expect it to get louder, while the offensive line and the play sheet get less airtime.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Broncos DB Devon Key awarded wild interception in the Panthers' end zone after Denver challenge
articles.summary: The play had to be reviewed to confirm that the ball bounced off the hand of Carolina TE Tommy Tremble before Key plucked it out of the air.
articles.body:
In Sunday's matchup between the Carolina Panthers and Denver Broncos, a dropped touchdown pass turned into an unbelievable interception thanks to a well-timed challenge, a key play in Denver's tight road victory.

Toward the end of the third quarter, Panthers quarterback Bryce Young threw a pass to tight end Tommy Tremble in the end zone. Though the ball ended up in the hands of Broncos defensive back Devon Key, it looked like it hit the ground first, leading officials to rule the play incomplete.

Denver used its challenge flag, leading to a review that proved successful for the Broncos. As Tremble went down while trying to make the catch, the ball rolled off his wrist before bouncing off his hand, with Key in just the right position to pluck it out of the air. It never actually hit the ground, leading officials to overturn the call and rule it a Denver pick.

Because the play was ruled dead, Key did not get a chance to make a return, but the Broncos were given a touchback. Quarterback Bo Nix then led the team down the field on a 14-play, 80-yard touchdown drive to take a 19-15 lead, after Denver's 2-point conversion attempt was unsuccessful.

The game stayed tight until the end. Though the Broncos scored another fourth-quarter touchdown shortly afterward, the Panthers came back with Young finding Tetairoa McMillan in the end zone on the next drive.

A three-and-out Denver drive gave Carolina a late chance for a go-ahead touchdown, but Nik Bonitto forced Young's second turnover of Sunday with a sack and fumble recovery. The Broncos (7-2) then rode out the final minute and change for a 26-21 win .

articles.title: In 2022, Tyreek Hill spent $6.9 million on a luxurious Florida estate; but a devastating fire left him facing $2.3 million in damages
articles.summary: Tyreek Hill, the former Miami Dolphins’ wide receiver, has been going through a tough time in his life as he struggles to find a new team in the middle of
articles.body: Tyreek Hill, the former Miami Dolphins’ wide receiver, has been going through a tough time in his life as he struggles to find a new team in the middle of the season. While his career in the league remains uncertain, Tyreek Hill has made a new move for his mansion in Florida which he bought for $6.9 million and it had caught fire.Tyreek Hill's $6.9 million luxurious estate in Florida had caught fire as he desperately tried to sell it offIn 2022, the 32 year old popular wide receiver bought a 9,326 square foot, nine bedroom, 9.5 bathroom residence in Southwest Ranches, FL, on 2.28 acres ground.While the estate is luxurious, in 2024, the mansion had caught fire and had caused extensive damage to the property.According to AP news, the fire was caused by a child playing with a lighter but it was contained quickly by firefighters.In a report, Davie Fire Rescue Fire Marshal Robert Taylor said, "Thankfully, it was called in quickly enough that we were able to get to it and aggressively be able to contain the fire to the area…”While Tyreek Hill sought privacy then, his agent Drew Rosenhaus had opened up about the damage as he said, “He and his family are safe…No one was injured No. 1, no pets, so for that, we’re very grateful. We’re very grateful to the firefighters that put the fire out.”Tyreek Hill’s agent Drew Rosenhaus added, “Thankfully, the fire was contained to a limited area in the home. Obviously, there’ll be some smoke and water damage. It’s very difficult for anybody obviously to have your home catch on fire, but Tyreek was handling it, he and his family, with as much poise as you could hope.”Tyreek Hill rebuilt the house as he spent millions in damages but it fails to find a buyerDespite the financial loss, Tyreek Hill worked on his luxurious home again and rebuilt it as he spent $2.3 million in repairing it.According to the Realtor, the luxurious estate has a grand motor court while the main level features a home gym, wood paneled office, an open kitchen and a family room.Another floor features the primary suite attached to a luxe bathroom with a soaking tub, glass shower, and dual vanities. articles.title: Rams star Puka Nacua reportedly dealing with knee injury after win over Commanders, will undergo MRI
articles.summary: The Rams don't believe that Puka Nacua tore his ACL in their Week 9 win over the Commanders, but he will undergo further testing on Monday.
articles.body:
Los Angeles Rams star wide receiver Puka Nacua went down with a knee injury late in their 20-13 win over the Washington Commanders on Sunday .

Nacua is set to undergo an MRI on Monday to determine the severity of the injury, according to ESPN's Adam Schefter, though the team does not believe that he suffered a torn ACL.

Further specifics, including how long he may be sidelined, are not yet known.

Nacua caught a short pass with about 90 seconds left at Northwest Stadium, but was brought down well short of the line to gain. It didn't appear that anything went wrong in the moment, and Nacua jumped back up and left the field normally after being tackled.

Nacua had 150 yards and a touchdown on 14 catches in the win on Sunday. It marked his third outing this season with at least 125 receiving yards, and he's now scored a touchdown in four of his past five games.

The Rams rallied after falling into an early hole on Sunday to take the seven-point win. Nacua got his touchdown in the fourth quarter of the game on a 7-yard catch from Matthew Stafford, which put them up for good. Nacua somehow managed to make the grab almost through Commanders cornerback Trey Amos in the back of the end zone, too.

While it appears Nacua has avoided a major injury, losing him for any significant amount of time will undoubtedly make things much more difficult for the Rams as they try to mount a playoff push.

They've now won three straight, and will enter next week's matchup with the Arizona Cardinals with a 5-4 record. It's the first time they've been above .500 this fall, too. The Rams do have a bye in Week 11, however, which would give Nacua extra time to recover.

But until his MRI comes back on Monday and the Rams have a clearer picture, his status moving forward is now very much unknown.

articles.summary: The Kansas City Current’s rapid rise has brought fresh attention to the club’s home, CPKC Stadium.
articles.body: The Kansas City Current’s rapid rise has brought fresh attention to the club’s home, CPKC Stadium. But a proposed $1.4 billion development around the riverfront sparked a debate in July 2026. The ambitious project promised a bigger matchday experience, better connections and new attractions. However, its request for as much as $235 million in public bonds raised questions about who should pay for the transformation. With Patrick Mahomes and Brittany Mahomes among the club’s high-profile owners, the proposal also put the spotlight on the Current’s future in Kansas City.KC Current stadium expansion plan puts public funding under scrutinyThe proposed development aimed to turn the Berkley Riverfront into a larger sports and entertainment destination. Plans included additional seating at CPKC Stadium, new restaurants, improved walking and cycling trails, a parking garage and a pedestrian bridge linking the River Market to the stadium.New designs released by the Kansas City Current and architecture firm Gensler on June 30 offered a glimpse of how the district could change. The bridge, in particular, drew interest from people who regularly travel through the area.Tori Carter, who works nearby, welcomed the idea of separating pedestrian movement from road traffic. “A bridge would be so big — it’s kind of just annoying when you’re driving and you’ve got to wait for people crossing, so a bridge would be huge,” Carter said.Some residents also viewed the expansion as a natural next step for a neighbourhood that has changed significantly since the stadium opened. Azealia Dixon, who had lived in the area for three years, said the project could bring more activities and visitors to the city.“I think it’s awesome. It brings a lot of people to Kansas City — more expansion, more fun, more things to do. And it’s local too and it’s convenient now so everyone kind of has the opportunity to come,” Dixon said.Patrick Mahomes and Brittany Mahomes’ KC Current expansion faces mixed reactionThe biggest point of disagreement was not the proposed construction itself, but the financing. The plan asked Kansas City to support up to $235 million in public bonds. Mayor Quinton Lucas backed the request, but the proposal still needed full City Council approval before formal negotiations could move forward.For some supporters, that funding request was difficult to accept. Danielle Russell, vice president of the KC Blue Crew supporters group, pointed to the club’s original promise of a privately financed stadium.“When the stadium was first announced, a big part of it was the privately financed aspect and how special that was,” Danielle Russell said.She remained interested in the improvements but admitted that public funding changed how some fans viewed the proposal.“While I think there’s a lot of feelings that of course you’re going to need a bond, of course it’s going to be taxpayers — that’s just how reality goes — there’s just this part that’s like, man, this stinks. It’s conflicting a bit,” she said.Patrick Mahomes and Brittany Mahomes are part of the KC Current ownership group, making the club’s long-term growth a notable part of the wider discussion. Still, the July proposal was not a completed deal. City officials also had parking and traffic concerns to review before the council could decide whether to advance it.The expansion offered a major vision for the riverfront, but its future depended on whether Kansas City could agree on how to pay for it.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Giants' win over Eagles wasn't pretty, but it didn't need to be for NFC East's team to beat
articles.summary: The temptation is surely there to buff up the Giants' roster via trade but John Harbaugh has stressed that the Giants aren't in the market for a quick fix.
articles.body:
There's nothing quite like breaking a long streak of futility. Sometimes it's a world championship drought, and sometimes it's as simple as a 13-year run of failure in your opponent's house.

The New York Giants won on Sunday in Philadelphia for the first time since before "Frozen" hit movie theaters. And somehow, despite injuries up and down the roster, Big Blue is now firmly in charge of the NFC East.

The Giants' resurgence is coinciding with the career rebirth of J.J. McCarthy, who shook off an apparent hip injury to lead New York to a 19-11 win. It wasn't pretty, and this isn't a graceful resurgence — less "bird of prey taking flight" and more "baby deer getting to its feet" — but when you're a member of the NFC East, you can limp your way to a division title.

McCarthy could follow in the footsteps of Sam Darnold, Baker Mayfield and Geno Smith, all of whom rejuvenated their careers with other teams than the ones that drafted them. But it's clear McCarthy — who was 12-of-19 passing for 127 yards — is finding more room to develop in New York than he did in Minnesota.

For a moment during the game, the Giants looked as snakebit as any franchise in the league. McCarthy looked like he suffered a severe hip injury , collapsing to the ground in pain after taking a vicious hit:

But he returned just two series later, during which Jameis Winston led New York to its only touchdown of the afternoon. Giants head coach John Harbaugh said he and his staff considered leaving Winston in for the rest of the game, but ultimately decided to go back to their starter.

"Trainers and the docs said he was good, and he said he was ready to go," Harbaugh said. "With that, we decided to put him back out there."

Behind McCarthy, the Giants' running back room remains a work in progress. Cam Skattebo missed the game with a hamstring injury; Devin Singletary got more carries Sunday (21) than he had all season to date (18), and Gregory Desrosiers jumped up from the practice squad to carry the ball three times for 20 yards. Those numbers would seem to suggest a possibility, perhaps even a mandate, for New York to make a deadline deal over the next 48 hours.

New York maintains a lead over Dallas, including a Week 1 victory, with both Philadelphia and Washington floundering. The temptation is surely there to buff up the Giants' roster via trade — perhaps through a running back like Jonathan Taylor — but Harbaugh has stressed that the Giants aren't in the market for a quick fix.

"It's got to make sense, short-term and long-term. We're not just going to go for a short-term fix at an exorbitant cost," Harbaugh said. "Usually, when you do that sort of thing, it doesn't work out for you. You end up paying a hefty price, and you don't get the return on it."

Harbaugh noted that the Giants are "making a lot of calls," but emphasized that he didn't think there was some franchise savior sitting around out there ready to complete the Giants' roster.

"I never think that you're one step away or one player away. To me, it's always just a total momentum kind of a thing anyway," he said. "But if the right opportunity comes, and there's a deal that makes sense for us, we'll do it."

Four days from now, the Giants will face Washington at home, and will follow that up with two against the AFC South's Jaguars and Colts. The Giants' remaining schedule ranks right in the middle of the league, per Tankathon , with the rest of the division clustered around them. That means the Giants won't be able to take advantage of any schedule breaks, and neither will the rest of the NFC.

Beyond that, well … the playoffs are murky and mysterious. There's not anything that New York does particularly well on offense, unsurprising given the quarterback inconsistency. The Giants' defense ranks ninth in the league in yards allowed, not spectacular but enough to keep New York in almost every game remaining on its schedule.

New York vanquished some Philly ghosts on Sunday, and McCarthy continues to gain valuable experience and playing time. The Giants are on track to get back to the playoffs for the first time since the 2022 season. Sure, they're not burning up that track, and they're making pit stops almost every week to change quarterbacks and running backs, but as long as they're the first one across the line, who really cares what they look like when they do?

articles.title: Josh Allen, the wing sauce diplomat: why one Buffalo restaurant owner uses his order to test new hires
articles.summary: Josh Allen's influence in Buffalo extends beyond the football field, and his reputation as a fan of chicken wings has become part of the city's restaurant
articles.body: Josh Allen's influence in Buffalo extends beyond the football field, and his reputation as a fan of chicken wings has become part of the city's restaurant culture. The Buffalo Bills quarterback has shared his favorite wing spots, discussed his preferred flavors and helped put local businesses in front of a wider audience. For one restaurant owner, Allen's order has even become an unusual way to judge new employees. It is a small detail, but it says plenty about how closely the city connects its football star with one of its most familiar food traditions.Josh Allen's Bar-Bill order has become part of the Buffalo routineJosh Allen's connection with Bar-Bill Tavern dates back to April 2018, when the Bills brought him to Buffalo for a pre-draft visit. He had dinner at the East Aurora restaurant with two Bills scouts and two members of the team's football operations department. What began as a meal during a visit that could shape his NFL future eventually turned into a regular habit.The quarterback found something he liked immediately. In a 2020 interview with The Ringer, Allen recalled that first experience and said, “It’s a spot that I fell in love with,” before adding, “I had the best wings I’ve ever had. I just, kind of, knew that it felt right here.”His regular order became almost as well known as his preference for the restaurant itself. Allen's combination included 10 Cajun honey-butter BBQ wings, 10 hot wings and shoestring fries with extra blue cheese. That is a fairly specific order, especially for someone who could easily visit a different restaurant every week.There was another version of his wing preference that he shared publicly in 2022. Speaking on Mad Dog Radio, Allen said, “I go Bar-Bill,” before explaining, “I get ten hot. And then to soothe that out, I get ten lemon pepper.” He also praised the restaurant for adding lemon pepper to its menu, calling it “freaking fantastic.”The change in his preferred flavors is worth noting. Allen has never appeared particularly interested in making his food choices complicated. He likes a mix of heat and milder flavors, with blue cheese alongside his wings. For a city where people can have strong opinions about how chicken wings should be served, that makes him a familiar kind of customer.His reputation also gives the restaurant a connection to one of the biggest names in Western New York sports. A regular customer recommending a restaurant is one thing. When that customer is the Bills' franchise quarterback, the recommendation carries a different level of attention.The order has become a small test of restaurant knowledgeFor the restaurant, Allen's popularity has created an interesting situation. His order is no longer just another ticket coming through the kitchen. It is familiar enough to serve as a practical test for new hires. Knowing what the Bills quarterback likes gives staff an easy way to show that they understand the restaurant's regular customers and the details that make its service personal.That might sound like a simple exercise, but it reflects how much attention a familiar customer can bring to a local business. A new employee does not need to know the quarterback personally. They need to understand the order, get the details right and recognise why it matters to the people who come through the door.Allen has also given Buffalo's wing scene attention beyond Bar-Bill. In January 2025, he appeared on former Bills centre Eric Wood's The Buffalo Pod and discussed his favourite places. Bar-Bill remained at the top of his list, with Mulberry Ristorante second and Wingnutz third. He had previously included La Nova in his top three, making Wingnutz the notable change.Then, in September 2025, Allen offered another ranking. Speaking after practice, he said, “I think everybody knows that Bar-Bill is probably my favorite,” before adding, “I think Mulberry’s has some sneaky good wings, and then obviously Wing Nutz is pretty dang good too.”He also encouraged visitors to explore the city's food options. "There's a lot of good options," said the Bills quarterback. "Any chance that you can go and try some new wings here, you should probably jump at the chance to do it."That endorsement carries value for Buffalo's restaurant owners. Allen has spent years building a connection with the city, and his willingness to talk about local food gives businesses exposure that conventional advertising cannot easily replicate.There is a personal side to this relationship, too. Allen's first Bar-Bill visit came before the Bills drafted him, at a point when Buffalo was still one of several possible NFL destinations. The restaurant became part of his early experience of the city. Years later, his food preferences are familiar enough to feature in conversations about the local dining scene.For a restaurant owner, having the quarterback's order remembered by employees is a useful detail. It turns a celebrity connection into something tangible at the counter. And in Buffalo, where football and chicken wings share a place in everyday conversation, Josh Allen has managed to become part of both.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Jonathan Taylor says he's 'grateful' for time in Indy after what could be his last game with Colts
articles.summary: INDIANAPOLIS (AP) — Indianapolis Colts running back Jonathan Taylor was warming up Sunday when the two large stadium video boards began showing a montage of...
articles.body:
INDIANAPOLIS (AP) — Indianapolis Colts running back Jonathan Taylor was warming up Sunday when the two large stadium video boards began showing a montage of his highlights.

It wasn't necessarily a send-off, but after weeks of speculation about Taylor's potential trade value , it sure felt like he might be playing his final home game at Lucas Oil Stadium.

After the Colts lost 27-23 to the Dallas Cowboys , the 2021 NFL rushing champ acknowledged that his 6 1/2 seasons in Indy could be coming to an end. The NFL trade deadline is Tuesday, and it's possible that Indy could move Taylor, quarterback Daniel Jones or both.

"I think you play every game like it's your last. But at the end of the day, this has been a spot where I've grown up," Taylor said. "After college, you're trying to grow up, you're starting a family, and you really embrace this city and the people. You're just like, 'This place helped shape me into the man I am today.' I'm very grateful for the city of Indianapolis."

If this was the end for Taylor and the Colts (2-7), it was memorable for the wrong reasons.

Indy overcame a 10-point second-half deficit to take a 23-20 lead with 1:37 left, then watched as the Cowboys answered right back with Javonte Williams' 1-yard TD run. A late interception sealed the Colts' fifth straight loss.

Taylor never got much going. He rushed 13 times for 46 yards but the franchise's career leader in TD runs (77) didn't find the end zone. He added five receptions for 18 yards and lost a fourth-quarter fumble that cost Indy (2-7) a key scoring chance.

While the Colts have already traded away multiple players as they collect draft picks and clear salary cap space for 2027, Taylor has kept his focus on the task at hand — an approach coach Shane Steichen has appreciated.

Steichen, whose own job is in jeopardy, wasn't ready to say goodbye, either.

"I'm not going to get into any trade speculation. He's on our football team," Steichen said, referring to Taylor.

It's not just Taylor who could be dealt.

Jones has struggled with turnovers this season after starting his Colts career in 2025 with 10 impressive games. He was benched during last week's 42-7 drubbing at Jacksonville, which contributed to the trade speculation.

Jones didn't play to his standard Sunday, either. He was 20 of 34 for 180 yards with two TDs and one interception — a pick by Caleb Downs with 35 seconds left that sealed the game.

Jones said he hasn't thought much about a potential trade.

"There have been plenty of distractions the last couple weeks with all the stuff that's gone on, and it's unfortunate we're in that position," Jones said. "But I think as players, your job is to focus as much on what's in front of you. And playing quarterback, there's a lot focusing on getting ready for a game. So that was my approach."

Receiver Josh Downs, meanwhile, is ready for a change. He caught only three passes for 24 yards while playing against his younger brother Caleb Downs, but unlike Taylor or Jones, Downs requested a trade last week.

"I'm open to whatever," he said. "If they want me to stay here, I'll be here. If they don't, and they want to trade me away, they'll trade me away."

That's not how Jones or Taylor seem to feel, but they may not be around next week when the Colts host rebuilding Miami. In Taylor's case, he'd like to keep producing highlights with the only NFL team he's played for.

"I love repping the horseshoe, but it's out of our control now," he said. "The hay is in the barn. We just play the waiting game now."

articles.title: Packers Winners and Losers: Week 9 vs. the Patriots
articles.summary: The Packers are picking up steam as they dominate the reigning AFC champion Patriots.
articles.body:
The Green Bay Packers traveled to face off against the New England Patriots on Sunday afternoon, and they were in control the entire time. With a commanding 45-27 win over the reigning AFC champions, the Packers find themselves 6-3 after 9 weeks of play. Let's dive in and take a look at what worked this week.

S Xavier McKinney logged his second multi-interception game of the season, and that's about enough to name him a winner this week. McKinney is up to 5 picks on the season, his most since 2024 (8).

WR Matthew Golden had 6 catches for 126 yards…by the end of the first quarter. Not only is this a career high in a game for Golden, but it's also the most receiving yards by any player in one quarter so far this season. He was wide open, pretty much at all times, which led to big gain after big gain.

We saw firsthand on Sunday exactly why the Packers selected Golden in the first round of the draft last year. As a result of his growing chemistry with his quarterback, he had the honor of becoming the answer to the trivia question "Who caught Jordan Love's 100th career TD pass?"

Golden finished the day catching all 10 targets for 164 yards and 1 TD. And the WR success didn't stop with him.

Death. Taxes. WR Christian Watson was wide open. Watson showed us some gorgeous stuff on Sunday, including this one-handed catch which he made look absolutely effortless.

He had another incredible catch later in the game to get the Packers close to the endzone (I think this should've been ruled a TD, but IT'S FINE, I'M FINE).

Watson finished the day catching 7 of 8 targets for 171 yards and 1 TD. Who needs Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins when you have Christian Watson and Matthew Golden?

If S Evan Williams isn't First Team All-Pro by the end of this season, something has gone very, very wrong. He was all over the field on Sunday: getting after Patriots QB Drake Maye and forcing quick throws, making big tackles at the point of catch, and coming down with one of the most impressive interceptions I've seen all year. I mean, look at this!

We all held our breath as he was slow to get up after a scary play in the second half, but he came back into the game and continued right where he left off: haunting Drake Maye. Williams finished the day with 5 tackles, 1 INT, and 1 PD. It all started to make sense when Tom Brady announced during the broadcast that Williams' mom, Dani, babysat Brady when he was a child. Brady clearly got his power from Dani Williams, and so did Evan.

For the first time this season, we finally get to say THE PACKERS RUN GAME HELPED THEM OUT TODAY, kind of. The offense had 129 yards on the ground today, and Kaleb Johnson accounted for 68 of them on 14 carries. He had the team's biggest run of the day with a 34 yarder to open the 4th quarter. Also, Baby's First Touchdown!

SMACK IS BACK (for now). After a rough couple of weeks which caused me to make an emergency visit to my hair colorist to get rid of some grays, the Packers rookie K was perfect against the Patriots. He made all 4 XPs, and made 3 more FGs, with a long of 51. Let's do this again next week.

Do you hear that? The MVP chants…they're getting louder. QB Jordan Love was absolutely incredible on Sunday. He used his legs to escape a collapsing pocket, and scored the team's first TD of the game. From there, it was nothing but the Air Show. The unfortunate victim this week was the NFL's highest paid DB, Christian Gonzalez. Love picked a good time to be a walking highlight reel. Here you go:

Please remain seated; we're not finished.

Love finished the day 23 of 29 (79%) for 372 yards and 3 passing TDs, with another 13 yards and 1 TD on the ground, for a 153.2 rating.

The RB finished the day with 4 carries for 5 yards before exiting with a hand injury. He also pled no contest to battery in September after a May 2026 incident involving his former girlfriend.

Despite being 6-3, the Packers are sitting at the bottom of the toughest division in football, leaving little room for error as they head into the second half of the season. Next week is a big one, as they head back home to face off against the Minnesota Vikings, who are 6-1 at the time of publication. After an embarrassing Week 1 loss to Minnesota, can the Packers redeem themselves and flip the NFC North on its head in the process?

articles.title: The 1 trade Lions must make in final week before 2026 NFL trade deadline
articles.summary: The Detroit Lions picked up an easy win in Week 9. Detroit cruised to a lazy 19-9 victory over Miami just before the NFL trade deadline. Now the Lions find...
articles.body:
The Detroit Lions picked up an easy win in Week 9 . Detroit cruised to a lazy 19-9 victory over Miami just before the NFL trade deadline. Now the Lions find themselves at 6-2 on the season and right in the thick of the NFC North division race. If Detroit can continue to stack wins, they'll have a good chance of making the playoffs this winter.

If there's one area where Detroit needs to improve, it is certainly on defense. The Lions have depth issues in their secondary as usual. They are also dealing with linebacker problems after losing Jack Campbell for the foreseeable future with a scary neck injury. Plus DJ Wonnum, Mekhi Wingo, and a host of other players are dealing with lingering injuries.

The return of Kerby Joseph should help a little bit. But the Lions would be wise to consider adding some reinforcements at the deadline. They could be just one or two defensive players away from having a truly dangerous roster.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

So will the Lions make a move at the deadline? And if so, who might they have their eyes on?

This is one trade that the Lions need to pull off before the 2026 NFL trade deadline.

The Lions need to reunite with cornerback Carlton Davis at the trade deadline

Here are the terms of this hypothetical trade before getting into any of the analysis.

Davis is certainly a player the Lions need to keep an eye on.

Albert Breer of Sports Illustrated named Davis as a player to watch ahead of the deadline. The Patriots have not given any signals that they are trying to trade Davis, but they could be persuaded with the right offer.

Still, head coach Mike Vrabel downplayed the trade rumors during an interview ahead of Week 9.

"This time of year, I think that all these things kind of get drummed up," Vrabel said, per Nicole Yang of the Boston Globe. "So, we're focused on trying to prepare for Green Bay and make the corrections from the game. This is business as normal here, so I don't know where a lot of these things come from. Certainly not from any conversations with me."

One reason to believe in this deal is New England's financial position. The Patriots don't have much cap space in future seasons, so making gains anywhere they can should be a priority. New England likely won't get much from the compensatory pick formula this year either, so reinforcements aren't automatically on the way.

If the Patriots trade away Davis, they'll gain $16.5 million in cap space this year and in 2027. That could help New England a lot, especially after paying Christian Gonzalez $135 million this offseason.

Meanwhile, Rakestraw will still be under contract in 2027. He would give the Patriots a cheap, high-upside option at cornerback.

The combination of cap savings, draft pick, and young player would make this offer tempting for New England's front office.

Would Carlton Davis fix Detroit's secondary issues?

That explains why the Patriots might consider trading Davis back to the Lions. But does this trade make much sense for Detroit? And more importantly, would it solve their defensive issues?

The Lions desperately need to add bodies on the boundary. Davis checks that box and would give Detroit two solid starters between him and D.J. Reed. This does not magically fix all of Detroit's problems, but it does make their starting lineup much more competitive. In fact, it makes their defense downright viable against playoff-caliber offenses.

Davis has some familiarity with defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard. After all, he did spent a season in Detroit's defense in 2024. Sheppard's scheme is different from Aaron Glenn's, but similar enough that Davis could probably get up to speed pretty fast.

Lions fans already know that Davis is a playmaker on defense. One knock on him is his availability. Davis has missed multiple games with a neck injury in 2026. He's still the same player when available, but the Lions could be spooked by that neck injury. Especially after Campbell's neck injury from last week.

The most awkward part about this trade is that it would have to happen just before Week 10. That means Davis would be changing teams just before an international game in Germany between the two teams.

This trade seems to make a lot of sense for both teams. However, that upcoming international game may be just enough friction to keep a trade like this from happening.

Regardless, players like Davis are exactly who Lions fans should be praying for ahead of the trade deadline on Tuesday afternoon.

articles.title: Myles Garrett on three-sack game: It was a weight off my shoulders to get back to who I am
articles.summary: Myles Garrett was Myles Garrett on Sunday.
articles.body:
Myles Garrett was Myles Garrett on Sunday.

Now healthy, Garrett made three sacks and had six pressures on 27 pass rushes in the Rams' 20-13 win over Washington, according to NFL Next Gen Stats.

"Man, it was a weight off my shoulders , just getting back to who I am," Garrett said, via Sarah Barshop of ESPN. "I'm nowhere near where I want to be as far as my performance and things I know I can do and how I can move, but this is a confidence booster for sure."

Garrett tried to play through a knee injury in Week 1 and had no stats in 40 snaps. He underwent arthroscopic surgery the following week and had not played again until Sunday.

Garrett called his Week 1 performance "the worst version of myself that I put out there."

Sunday marked the ninth time Garrett has had three sacks, and the reigning Defensive Player of the Year now has 128.5 sacks in his NFL career.

The Rams traded what they traded for Garrett for him to be the closer they haven't had since Aaron Donald initially retired in the 2024 offseason. He did just that in his second game.

"I am that closer, so we don't need to look any further," Garrett said.

It was the first game Garrett and Donald played together. They were on the field at the same time for 23 plays and combined for four sacks.

articles.title: Russell Wilson’s NC State hopes crushed as Philip Rivers closes in on head coach job amid former Seahawks star’s CBS career shift
articles.summary: Russell Wilson appeared to have an unexpected chance to return to NC State, but his hopes of becoming the Wolfpack's next head coach are fading.
articles.body: Russell Wilson appeared to have an unexpected chance to return to NC State, but his hopes of becoming the Wolfpack's next head coach are fading. The university is reportedly closing in on Philip Rivers, another former quarterback with a strong connection to the program. The development puts Wilson's brief coaching opportunity in doubt and leaves his new career in television as his immediate focus.Wilson had interviewed for the job after retiring from the NFL, but Rivers now appears to have moved ahead in the race. The former Los Angeles Chargers star brings something Wilson does not: six seasons of experience as a head coach. Philip Rivers emerges as NC State's top choice over Russell WilsonAccording to On3's Chris Low, Pete Nakos and Noah Fleischman, NC State is finalising an agreement with Rivers to become its next head coach. The report surfaced on November 8, just two days after Rivers' high school team saw its season end.Rivers spent the past six seasons coaching St. Michael Catholic High School in Fairhope, Alabama. His team lost 42-35 to Glenwood in the first round of the Alabama state playoffs on November 6. The defeat brought his high school coaching campaign to an end and opened the door for a possible return to college football.Speaking to WRAL after the game, Rivers reflected on what he had achieved with the programme."We didn’t have a stadium a few years ago. If it were to be the last time out here, shoot, a lot was accomplished."Rivers also has a strong connection to NC State. He played for the Wolfpack from 2000 to 2003 and finished his college career with 13,484 passing yards and 95 touchdowns. He remains one of the most celebrated quarterbacks in the programme's history.There is another reason why his potential appointment has attracted attention. His son, Gunner Rivers, is a four-star quarterback recruit in the 2027 class who committed to NC State in February. That could create an unusual father-son connection in Raleigh if the hiring goes through.However, the university's Board of Trustees still needs to review and approve the contract terms before NC State can officially announce Rivers as its next head coach. Russell Wilson's coaching opportunity takes a hit after NC State interviewWilson had also emerged as a serious candidate for the position. The former Seattle Seahawks quarterback played for NC State from 2008 to 2010 and made a lasting impression during his time there.In 2008, he became the first freshman quarterback in the 55-year history of the ACC to earn First-Team All-ACC honours. His college achievements made a possible return to Raleigh an interesting prospect.ESPN's Adam Schefter reported on November 3 that Wilson had interviewed for the vacant head coaching position. The news came as a surprise, considering Wilson had only recently stepped away from his playing career.During an appearance on NBC's Today With Jenna & Sheinelle, Wilson addressed the possibility of coaching his former college team."Well, listen, when your alma mater calls, you always answer. Listen, I love doing what I’m doing."Wilson's response showed that he was open to hearing from NC State, although he also expressed his interest in his current television career. He joined CBS Sports as an analyst on The NFL Today after retiring in June 2026 following 14 NFL seasons.The coaching experience also gave Rivers an advantage. Wilson has never coached at any level, while Rivers has spent six seasons managing a high school programme and developing young players.NC State opened the position after firing Dave Doeren on October 24. Doeren finished his 14-season tenure with 98 victories, the most by any head coach in programme history.Now, the Wolfpack appear close to choosing Rivers over Wilson. While the former Seahawks star's interview briefly raised the possibility of an NFL-to-college coaching move, his immediate future remains in the CBS studio. Rivers, meanwhile, could soon return to the programme where his own college football journey began.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: “I think it's disrespectful”: Shedeur Sanders under fire as New Orleans Saints star calls out Cleveland Browns QB’s cryptic comments after OT loss
articles.summary: Cleveland Browns quarterback Shedeur Sanders had plenty to prove in his first start of the 2026 NFL season.
articles.body: Cleveland Browns quarterback Shedeur Sanders had plenty to prove in his first start of the 2026 NFL season. But his pregame comments about the New Orleans Saints defense caught the attention of defensive end Carl Granderson. After Sunday's 23-22 overtime loss on November 8, Granderson made his feelings clear, calling Sanders' reaction disrespectful. The Saints defender also had a strong performance to back up his words.Sanders had smiled when reporters asked about his preparation for New Orleans. That reaction sparked questions about how the Saints would respond on the field. They eventually made life difficult for the young quarterback, and Granderson had a major role in their defensive effort. Carl Granderson takes issue with Shedeur Sanders’ reaction to Saints defenseThe tension started before the Week 9 matchup at Caesars Superdome. During a press conference ahead of the November 8 game, Sanders was asked what he had seen while studying the Saints defense."I've seen a lot," the Browns quarterback replied with a smile. He then added, "When I smile, just know that means something. I'm maturing, you know what I'm saying? I'm maturing."Sanders did not directly criticise New Orleans, but his response caught the attention of the Saints. Granderson addressed the exchange during his postgame press conference after the 23-22 victory."We seen a lot on film," the defensive end said when asked if Sanders' comments had motivated the team. "I don't think we're motivated, though. We seen him chirping. We just came into this game like, ready to play, win the game on defense."However, Granderson did not hide his frustration with the quarterback's reaction."I think it's disrespectful for somebody to laugh at our defense, take us as a joke. So, we went out there and balled out," he added.The Saints had another reason to make their point. Their defense entered the game ranked 28th in total yards allowed, according to the pregame figures cited in the original report. Yet the unit delivered when Cleveland needed points most. Saints defense answers with five sacks before stopping Browns in overtimeGranderson did more than speak about the exchange. He recorded two sacks against Sanders, while the Saints defense finished with five. New Orleans also limited Cleveland to 95 rushing yards on 34 attempts, giving the Browns fewer options to support their passing game.The defensive effort became even more important in overtime. New Orleans took the lead through a 15-yard touchdown pass from quarterback Tyler Shough to tight end Juwan Johnson with 4:17 remaining. Cleveland needed a touchdown and a successful two-point conversion to win.Sanders gave the Browns a chance. He connected with tight end Harold Fannin Jr. for a 39-yard touchdown with one minute left in overtime. However, the two-point attempt proved costly.Granderson applied pressure as Sanders rolled to his right and forced an incomplete pass intended for wide receiver Denzel Boston. An offensive holding penalty against tackle Tytus Howard also complicated the attempt. The Saints held on for a 23-22 win.Sanders still had an impressive statistical outing despite the defeat. He completed 19 of 31 passes for 297 yards and two touchdowns. Earlier, he connected with rookie wide receiver KC Concepcion Jr. for a 64-yard touchdown that gave Cleveland a 13-9 lead in the fourth quarter.The quarterback also addressed the controversy after the game. Speaking to reporters following the loss, Sanders said his words had been taken out of context."I was never, ever throwing a shot," Sanders explained. "I apologize if my words were taken out of context. I was never speaking negatively on anybody."The result gave New Orleans its first home victory of the 2026 season and improved its record to 3-5. Cleveland, meanwhile, fell to 5-4 after suffering its second consecutive defeat.In Granderson’s case, the final defensive stop offered a much better response than another exchange at the microphone. Sanders had shown flashes of what he could do in his first start, but the Saints made sure his comeback attempt ended without the result he wanted.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Caleb Williams’ health-first approach is changing his Bears season, and it all starts with what he eats
articles.summary: Caleb Williams has dropped 10 to 15 pounds since last season, and the Bears quarterback says the change started in his kitchen and his bedtime routine,
articles.body: Caleb Williams has dropped 10 to 15 pounds since last season, and the Bears quarterback says the change started in his kitchen and his bedtime routine, not just on the practice field. He stopped eating late at night, set regular meal times and made sleep a priority. He also reworked his training schedule. The aim is to move better on the field. Williams returned from a three-week injury absence and has played at a high level since, and Chicago has been playing well this season, so the new habits are getting a real test.Caleb Williams’ health-first approach starts with what he eatsWilliams explained the change to reporters during the offseason, and his answer had more routine than science in it. Meals at set times. A cutoff in the evening. Steady eating, not extremes. He laid out the rules to the Chicago Tribune.“Eating at certain times,” Williams said. “Going to bed and not eating after 7. Just eating consistently, eating well.”That sounds easy on paper. It rarely is. An NFL week is packed with film sessions, travel, treatment and games, and a 7 p.m. cutoff has to survive all of it. A cutoff also forces planning. Dinner has to happen on time, and late-night snacking has to stop. Williams is not chasing a trick here. He is building habits he can repeat every single week.Food was only one piece. He also changed how his training is set up, working out the right way and the right time to train, and he gave rest more room. Sleep now sits next to nutrition and training as a core part of the plan.It stands out because Williams tends to keep his personal life private. On food and sleep, he has been open.Bears are seeing the payoff from Williams’ workThe number on the scale is not really the point. Williams has a specific target for this season, and it has to do with how he moves.“I’m excited about that,” Williams said. “Being able to move a little better, be smoother.”Mobility matters for a quarterback whose job often depends on extending plays and staying upright for a full season. Lighter legs and a rested body help with both.The Bears have reason to like the direction. A quarterback who is available every week gives the offense a steadier base, and availability is a skill of its own. Arm talent does nothing from the training room.The early returns look good. Since coming back from the injury, Williams has been on a tear, and the team has played well around him. Nobody can say how much of that comes from a 7 p.m. kitchen cutoff. Football is never that clean.Still, a quarterback who feels lighter, sleeps more and moves with ease has fewer problems to solve on Sundays. And he already knows what missing games feels like. Staying on the field is the whole point.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.
