articles.title: They are last place in their own division — and a legitimate Super Bowl contender
articles.summary: The Green Bay Packers may be at the bottom of the NFC North division, but Jordan Love has them surging toward the postseason.
articles.body: The Green Bay Packers remained in last place in the NFC North despite beating the New England Patriots on Sunday. But that doesn’t mean anyone will be eager to play them anytime soon. The Packers dismantled the Patriots in their Week 9 matchup, winning 45-27 in a dominant showing. Green Bay quarterback Jordan Love had an MVP-level performance, completing 23 of 29 passes for 372 yards and three touchdowns. The Packers’ defense also played well, picking off Drake Maye three times. “That was a total team victory,” Green Bay head coach Matt LaFleur said postgame. “Each phase contributed in a large way.” Playing in a division in which every team has at least six wins has the Packers at the bottom of the NFC North. Yet they are every bit as dangerous, if not more, than some of the teams ahead of them. Love is a major reason Green Bay should be taken seriously as a Super Bowl contender. Playing behind a questionable offensive line, Love entered Sunday ranked 10th in QBR and has been the league’s top deep-shot thrower. He entered Sunday first in passes of both 20-plus yards and 40-plus yards, and he carved New England up with big play after big play. Love completed a 49-yard pass on the Packers’ second drive, a 43-yard pass on their third drive and then a 23-yard strike, followed by another 43-yard shot, on Green Bay’s final touchdown drive before halftime. Coupled with Maye’s turnovers, Love’s passing pushed the Packers to a 24-7 lead after two quarters. In the second half, Love completed throws of 28 yards, 33 yards and 39 yards (for a score) before he was ultimately removed from the game in the fourth with Green Bay holding a 45-21 lead. “I can’t say enough about the play of Jordan Love. He makes my job a hell of a lot easier,” LaFleur said. He added, in regard to his quarterback’s deep passing, “Those are low-percentage throws in theory, but he’s making them look high-percentage.” Love said he appreciated the aggressiveness of his coach’s game plan, commending him for continuing to dial up big plays. “It definitely felt like a real fun game to be part of,” he said. Packers receivers Matthew Golden and Christian Watson deserve their fair share of the credit for the offense’s success, as well. They each had at least 160 receiving yards against the Patriots. Watson caught seven balls for 171 yards and a score, while Golden added 10 receptions for 164 yards and a touchdown of his own. Love is on pace to shatter his career high in passing yards. He threw for 4,159 yards in 2022. At his current rate, he’ll throw for 4,945 if he plays in all 17 games. The Packers have been able to light teams up despite having an inefficient rushing attack. Green Bay entered Sunday ranked last in expected points added per rush, according to Sumer Sports. The Packers had only 485 yards rushing all season before Sunday’s win, fewest in the NFL and more than 100 yards fewer than the 31st-ranked Houston Texans. That means Love has had to carry the offense on his shoulders, and he has delivered. “He’s standing in there, he’s taking hits, and he’s still dealing the ball,” LaFleur said, adding that he would agree that Love is playing at an MVP level. Meanwhile, the defense has held up its end of the bargain. Green Bay went into Week 8 ranked in the top 10 in EPA per play defensively, and it was ranked in the top seven against both the run and the pass. On Sunday, the Packers forced Maye into one of his worst performances of the season. After having thrown only two interceptions in his last five starts, Maye threw for three alone against Green Bay. The Packers now lead the NFL with 13 picks. There’s no question Green Bay has the talent on both sides of the ball to be formidable in the postseason, but making it there will be an uphill climb. The Packers came out of Sunday’s game in the seventh and final playoff spot in the NFC, with the rest of the NFC North ahead of them and two 5-4 teams who made the playoffs a year ago (the Los Angeles Rams and the defending champion Seattle Seahawks) behind them. Green Bay will at least have a chance to make up ground in the division next weekend, as it will host the first-place Minnesota Vikings. “We gotta be able to regroup,” Love said. “The mindset just has to be complete focus and preparation on Minnesota. It’s all about getting back to work.”

articles.title: Kansas City Chiefs avoid a Patrick Mahomes nightmare, yet the road ahead is more complicated than the early good news suggests
articles.summary: Patrick Mahomes took a hard hit late in the second quarter of Sunday’s 35-12 win over the Jets, and Arrowhead went silent.
articles.body: Patrick Mahomes took a hard hit late in the second quarter of Sunday’s 35-12 win over the Jets, and Arrowhead went silent. Defensive end David Bailey caught him mid-throw, forcing a sack-fumble. Mahomes grabbed at his right arm and needed help getting to the sideline. He still returned for the next series and played most of the second half. Andy Reid called it an injury to the “elbow region,” and Mahomes said more testing is coming. Kansas City got the win and some early good news. The full diagnosis is still unknown.Chiefs wait on test results after Mahomes’ arm injuryThe play looked ugly in real time. Patrick Mahomes was winding up on second-and-10 when Bailey got to him. The ball came out, and Jets edge rusher Will McDonald fell on it in Kansas City territory. Mahomes stayed down for a moment, then reached for his right arm.Nobody at Arrowhead needed a reminder of last year. Mahomes tore his ACL less than a year ago, on that same field. A quarterback clutching a limb carries a different weight there, even when the damage turns out small.He came back anyway.Mahomes said he did not feel like he was throwing “the way” he wanted after halftime, though that improved with reps. Justin Fields only entered to kneel out the final minutes. That means Mahomes worked through it for most of the second half. He also admitted the exact spot on his arm is still unclear. Testing will answer that.His stance was simple. “If I’m able to play, I’m going to play,” Mahomes said. “That’s part of the game, that’s part of playing. It scares you in moments where you get some pains in certain areas of your body.”Reid points to Mahomes’ toughness as a team-wide liftReid said his mind went straight to the backup. “Get Justin ready,” Reid said. “Quickly. That’s kind of where you’re at on the field.”Reid said he did not know Mahomes would return until the series was about to start. “But he’s a tough kid. If there’s any way he can come back from something, he’s coming back.”Mahomes has played through plenty over the years, and sometimes he has healed faster than expected. His biggest hurdle so far was that ACL tear.“When you have a quarterback that’s tough, it affects everybody,” Reid said. “Nobody does it better than he does it.”The scoreboard made it easy to forget the scare. Kansas City won 35-12 and barely sweated the second half. But Week 10 is next, and Mahomes said his attention is on the test results and getting ready for it.He expects to wake up sore. “I’m sure I’ll be sore tomorrow, but we’ll get right to it,” Mahomes said. The tests will say whether soreness is all it is.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: “He just showed unconditional love”: How Travis Kelce opened his home to help former Chiefs teammate Jody Fortson, who still calls him his favourite teammate ever
articles.summary: Travis Kelce had already established himself as one of the NFL's best tight ends when the Kansas City Chiefs signed Jody Fortson as an undrafted free
articles.body: Travis Kelce had already established himself as one of the NFL's best tight ends when the Kansas City Chiefs signed Jody Fortson as an undrafted free agent in 2019. Fortson was still learning the position, but he found a teammate who was willing to help him. Kelce shared his knowledge, explained the finer details of route-running and even invited him to his house to offer advice. Years later, Fortson revealed how much those gestures meant to him.The former Chiefs tight end had plenty of reasons to remember those years fondly. Kelce did not just help him understand football better. He made time for a young player who was trying to earn his place in the league. When Fortson spoke about that experience in March 2024, he made it clear that Kelce had left a lasting impression on him. Travis Kelce treated an undrafted Chiefs rookie like more than just a teammateFortson joined Kansas City in 2019, when Kelce was already an established star. Sharing a meeting room with the veteran gave him a chance to learn from one of the best tight ends in the game. However, Kelce did not simply expect him to pick things up by watching.On March 18, 2024, Fortson spoke to reporters after signing with the Miami Dolphins. Asked about his experience alongside Kelce, he said, "Let me just tell you: Travis Kelce is my favorite teammate of all-time. On any level: Pop Warner, high school, college, Travis Kelce is my favorite teammate."He explained what made Kelce's support so special: "Not only because he took his time trying to teach me the role of being the tight end but because of how a great person he is. He didn't even have to (do that)."Fortson also remembered the way Kelce shared his knowledge of the game."He just showed unconditional love and just knowledge for the game," he said.Watching Travis Kelce helped him understand how to attack different routes, read coverage and find openings in opposing defences."Being in a room with Kelce, it definitely set me forward light years of where I would have been had I not had him, arguably having the greatest of all-time in that room," Fortson explained. A visit to Travis Kelce's house gave Jody Fortson a lesson he never forgotSome of Travis Kelce's most valuable advice came outside the Chiefs' training facility. Fortson recalled visiting his teammate's house, where they discussed how to improve his route-running."I used to be rushing my routes and stuff, but like, even going to Kelce's house and like, 'Hey, man, you can slow it down. Like every route doesn't have to be a hundred miles an hour, you can kind of play with the tempo. You can maneuver it a little bit,'" Fortson recalled.He added that there were "a lot of different nuances of the game" he learned from Kelce.The advice was simple but important. Fortson began to understand that running every route at full speed was not always the best approach. Changing pace and reading defenders could help him create better opportunities.Fortson also praised Chiefs head coach Andy Reid during the same media availability. articles.title: Should Giants trade for Jonathan Taylor? What's next for Kirk Cousins, Chiefs WRs? NFL trade deadline questions emerge from Sunday's games
articles.summary: Taylor may help, albeit without seeming necessary, for the Giants to win the NFC East. Meanwhile, a league source thought a third-round pick would compel the...
articles.body:
The conversation began two minutes into the second half.

The New York Giants' running backs had carried the ball eight times for a net 8 yards at that point. They'd traversed negative 20 yards before contact, according to the broadcast's Next Gen Stats graphic.

So Fox color analyst Greg Olsen, who spent 14 years as an NFL tight end, knew the question fans would ask themselves: Should the Giants, leading a struggling NFC East, trade for a veteran running back?

"I think they got to press pause here and take a clean look at it," Olsen said.

"If you get hit in the backfield," play-by-play announcer Joe Davis agreed, "it doesn't matter who you are."

Olsen contextualized the Giants' running back interest against the Eagles signing Saquon Barkley in 2024.

"I like to say: Good backs don't make bad run games good," Olsen said. "Good backs — in Saquon's case, great backs — make good run games great. So typically you want to have the offensive line, you want to have the run scheme, you want to have that element, you want to have that box checked.

" Then you add a Jonathan Taylor or a Kenneth Walker or a Saquon Barkley. The examples of going that order of operations are the ones that typically work the best."

Whoever cuts film for the Giants leadership might want to include that audio.

The Giants have struggled to develop consistency in their run game this season as injuries have limited running backs Cam Skattebo, Tyrone Tracy Jr. and Devin Singletary. Add a season-ending injury to mobile starting quarterback Jaxson Dart and a benching earlier this season to Skattebo, and the Giants have compiled an effective rushing attack every other week this season. Their offensive line ranks 18th in run-block win rate, per ESPN's advanced metric .

On Sunday, facing an injured and reeling Eagles team without Skattebo (hamstring), the Giants rushed for 80 total yards including a combined 33 from quarterbacks J.J. McCarthy and Jameis Winston.

Would Taylor help? And perhaps more importantly: Is he worth the Christian McCaffrey-like return the Colts are seeking, which equates to roughly a 2027 second- , third- and fourth-round pick as well as a 2028 fifth?

"I'd say we're open for any kind of situation, but I will say this, things do change," Harbaugh said. "Things change from day to day. So it's not like one day you may do something and the next day something happens and it changes your position. I'm not saying that report's not true. Those conversations are taking place, and if something happens for any player, I can't talk about any player because they're with other teams right now.

"We're not ruling anything out, but I don't see anything particularly imminent right now either. So we'll see what happens."

Complicating matters might be McCarthy's health. McCarthy left the game in the third quarter with a hip injury suffered on a hit from linebacker Zack Baun, the quarterback returning but then limping after a scramble. He finished the game. But if the Giants' run game requires quarterback mobility to jell, is McCarthy — their current mobile option, with Dart out for the season — durable enough?

And if that's in question, is a haul of future draft capital worth spending during the first season of the Harbaugh era?

At 5-2-1, the Giants hold a comfortable 65% chance of making the playoffs, per Next Gen Stats .

But their wins have all come against sub-.500 teams. Their schedule will thicken after this week's Thursday division game against the Washington Commanders. Five of their following six opponents are currently better than .500.

Taylor may help, albeit without seeming necessary, for the Giants to win the division. Will an offense pairing Taylor with McCarthy or Winston, pending health, help the Giants win a playoff game? And if not, are the Giants better off re-exploring the position this spring, at a lower cost?

"Somebody's got to come out that you really want to trade for that makes sense," Harbaugh said. "It's got to make sense short term and long term. We're not just going to go for a short-term fix at an exorbitant cost …

"Usually when you do that sort of thing, it doesn't work out for you."

What else from Sunday may impact this week's trade deadline? Here are two more stories to keep an eye on:

How much longer will Kirk Cousins be in Vegas?

At this point, it seems more likely than not that Cousins will stay put in Vegas and the Raiders will spare rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza the gauntlet of Seattle Seahawks, Denver Broncos and Cleveland Browns defenses next on the Raiders' schedule.

Even after posting his worst game of the season in a Sunday loss to the San Francisco 49ers , Cousins is still valuable to head coach Klint Kubiak and the franchise. His 2,340 passing yards rank fifth in the league and his 97.1 passer rating ranks 12th.

The Raiders will not simply give away Cousins.

But after Monday night, a team could be increasingly eager to test the price.

A Vikings team with the No. 1-ranked scoring defense and No. 27-ranked scoring offense hosts a red-hot Buffalo Bills team on Monday night. Minnesota will have a chance to see the areas of its team that are ready to compete deep into the playoffs and the areas that are not.

To this point, offense — and especially quarterback — have been glaring weaknesses. Kyler Murray has completed 64.9% of pass attempts for 1,022 yards, five touchdowns and three interceptions while Carson Wentz has completed 59% for 276 yards, three touchdowns and no picks.

The Raiders, with Cousins, have posted 331 yards per game to the Vikings' 279.4. And Cousins already knows head coach Kevin O'Connell's Vikings system intimately after playing in it in 2022 and 2023.

One league source thought a third-round pick would compel the Raiders to send Cousins to Minnesota and move on to Mendoza, recouping capital for a player who won't net a compensatory pick if he leaves in the spring due to his contract structure. Two other league sources put Cousins' value as ranging from a fifth to a fourth, possibly with a conditional clause in the trade.

"That makes sense for them," a high-ranking AFC executive said of the Vikings. "It'd be low start-up cost because he understands the offense already. They have enough around him that it wouldn't be like he's shouldering everything.

"It shouldn't cost more than a fourth or a fifth given his age [38] and you're probably renting him. That's probably a fourth."

While Sunday marked Cousins' first game this year with more interceptions (three) than touchdowns (one), two league sources said they did not expect that to influence Cousins' value at all given his large sample size of work, the Vikings' familiarity with Cousins and the 49ers' known defensive strengths.

The Raiders slipping from playoff contention — they have just a 14% chance of making the postseason, per Next Gen Stats — could increase their interest in moving Cousins for the right price. Monday night's game could sway the Vikings' interest.

How badly do the Chiefs need receiver help?

Two weeks ago, the leading Chiefs receiver was Cyrus Allen with 18 receiving yards. Last week, the leader in the room was Rashee Rice with 53 yards. And this week, in a 35-12 win over the New York Jets, Rice's 49 led the room.

The Chiefs need help. Manufacturing a passing game with tight ends and running backs will limit their ceiling in a postseason run. Add a hamstring injury to Xavier Worthy on Sunday, and the offense's reliance on running back Kenneth Walker III makes it too vulnerable.

Patrick Mahomes' reliance on 37-year-old tight end Travis Kelce is not sustainable. And after an MRI confirmed Mahomes' elbow injury was a strain or sprain in severity, per NFL Network , the Chiefs can feel comfortable moving forward with a trade.

The Chiefs haven't hidden their interest in a receiver. Nine weeks into the season, the case for a trade is strong. They're 6-2 with a 92% chance to make the playoffs, per Next Gen Stats. Their run game is potent, their offense the second-most productive in the league. Only eight teams have allowed fewer yards on defense than the Chiefs' 307.9 per game, per TruMediaSports.

Who might elevate the pass-catching group?

The Jacksonville Jaguars' Brian Thomas Jr. likely offers the highest ceiling if Jacksonville is willing to trade him. That reality is unclear: While Thomas is averaging just 2.75 targets a game and playing just 43% of offensive snaps, the Jaguars might value him as a field-stretcher for now and insurance if their corps sustains an injury . League sources expect Thomas to cost roughly a third-round pick to compel the Jaguars to trade him, with that value ranging from a fourth to a second depending on how competitive the market is and whether the Jaguars could recoup something else they need (hello, defensive tackle) in return.

"If I'm them, I'm not giving away any talent, no matter how useful they are, as long as they're not a detriment from a behavior or execution standpoint," the high-ranking AFC executive said. "OK, he's underperforming being a first-round pick, fine. But you're an injury away from, OK, if he's not there, who's playing receiver?

"Your goals are much different than everybody else's. So I would only move that dude before the season is over … if the price is just too good."

Indianapolis Colts receiver Josh Downs and Tennessee Titans receiver Calvin Ridley appear to be lower-ceiling, available options. Cowboys receiver George Pickens should be worth calling on, though team owner Jerry Jones seems unlikely to budge. And then there's San Francisco 49ers receiver Brandon Aiyuk as well as former Chiefs and Dolphins receiver Tyreek Hill, who each have the potential to boom or bust with questions about their health and readiness to positively impact a team. Historically, the Chiefs have not been deterred by risk.

articles.title: 5 momentous plays in Week 9: Commanders fail late again, and Browns' gutsy OT call
articles.summary: The Commanders mishandled their chances against the Rams, and the Browns opted to go for the win in overtime but failed.
articles.body:
Sunday's early action didn't exactly stir up some hot Monday debate. Several games were blowouts, with only five decided by one score.

There were some fascinating close-game finishes, however, and a few non-one-score games whose fates could have looked far different had one or two plays gone the other way.

The Washington Commanders, frequent guests of this list, have ended up here again thanks to a few fateful late plays in their failed upset bid against the Los Angeles Rams.

The Browns lost their second straight, and it came down to a critical call by head coach Todd Monken late in overtime.

We also had one of the wilder interceptions you'll ever see … and to think that it almost didn't go down as a pick added to the drama.

Here are five of the more momentous plays from Sunday's early action:

The Commanders had their opportunities to beat the Rams, but a mix of stalled drives and a messy final play doomed them in the end.

After the Rams took a 20-13 lead early in the fourth on Puka Nacua's touchdown, Washington got the ball back multiple times but couldn't generate points. Two drives in the final five-plus minutes ended without scoring.

The botched final play was the talking point after the game went final. Jayden Daniels threw short of the end zone, with the Commanders at the Rams' 32-yard line, and the ball was lateraled several times before being recovered by the Rams.

Let's be clear: It wasn't a well-thought-out plan. The fact Daniels didn't throw either of his final two passes into the end zone, with no timeouts, is damning.

But the sequence that really turned the game came near the two-minute warning. With 2:31 remaining at the Rams' 38-yard line, Daniels took a 12-yard sack by Myles Garrett, one of three on the day for him . Washington head coach Dan Quinn opted to let the clock run down to the two-minute stoppage.

On fourth-and-17, Daniels' deep throw to Van Jefferson was broken up by the Rams' Emmanuel Forbes Jr. at the last second.

Forbes, a former Commander, was guilty of a bad penalty and was beaten for a touchdown by Jefferson earlier in the game. Washington had a target on him, but Forbes made the big play.

The Browns were a 2-point conversion away from a 6-3 record. The Saints had taken a seven-point lead in overtime Sunday at the Superdome, but Shedeur Sanders — starting for an injured Deshaun Watson — rallied the Browns with a touchdown pass of his own with one minute left in OT.

Then came the decision: kick or go for it?

Browns head coach Todd Monken opted to go for 2 and the win. The play was doomed from the start. Sanders' hurried pass fell incomplete, and for good measure, the Browns' Tytus Howard was flagged for holding.

If you want to argue the play-call, be my guest. It looked like Sanders tried to make something happen out of structure, but it just wasn't there.

But Monken's call? I was fine with it. It felt like an aggressive, but highly defensible decision given where the Browns were at. They failed to get in on a fourth-and-goal situation earlier in the game and turned it over again on downs early in the fourth quarter. The Saints were at home, and the Browns were fortunate even to be in overtime after the Saints took the lead with less than a minute remaining.

Had they opted to tie it, the Saints would have had a full minute left and two timeouts. Tyler Shough led a six-play, 55-yard TD drive that took only 50 seconds earlier in the game.

Monken went for the win, and it's hard to blame him for that.

Nik Bonitto's strip sack on the Panthers' final drive sealed Sunday's Broncos win over the Panthers. But Devon Key's end-zone interception was also a massive play — and the kind you have to see to believe.

Late in the third quarter, Carolina led, 14-13, and had first-and-goal at the Denver 1. Bryce Young threw to a diving Tommy Tremble in the left corner of the end zone, with the ball hitting Tremble's hands twice before being ruled incomplete.

But wait! Replay saw what many others watching on television likely did: Key somehow catching the ball before it touched the ground.

Key smiled after the play, apparently not knowing he actually caught the ball. The fact that he had to whip his body almost completely around to make the play also added a serious degree of difficulty to the act.

What's wild is that Carolina had actually snapped the ball for second-and-goal, with Chuba Hubbard stopped for no gain, but Broncos head coach Sean Payton's challenge flag had come out prior to that snap.

There was also more controversy with the play, as Panthers fans wanted Denver's Justin Strnad flagged for pass interference, but there was no call.

The pick prevented at least three points, and possibly seven. So instead of a 4-to-8 point lead for the Panthers, they were only up one — briefly. The Broncos went down and scored a touchdown on their ensuing drive. After missing the 2-point try, Denver then led, 19-14.

It was a massive momentum swing in the game and a big reason why the Broncos held on to win.

The Falcons were their own worst enemies in their 34-17 loss to the Bengals in Spain. Penalties were one of the biggest problems for Atlanta — especially one critical flag.

Early in the fourth quarter, the Falcons trailed, 31-17, but they had the ball at the Cincinnati 10-yard line, facing a third-and-2. Kyle Pitts Sr. was called for holding, pushing the ball back to the 20 and making it fourth-and-12. The pass was incomplete on the hold, so it didn't wipe anything out, but their decision would have been a lot different on fourth-and-2.

Falcons head coach Kevin Stefanski opted for the field goal with 11:27 left … but Nick Folk pushed a 38-yarder wide left. Atlanta marched 11 plays and 52 yards and got nothing out of it.

The Falcons were flagged 12 times for 88 yards in the game. Earlier in the contest, they reached the Bengals' 7-yard line before multiple offensive line flags pushed them back and compelled them to settle for a field goal.

Atlanta had other things it needed to clean up in the Spain game, but the penalties really cost the Falcons. They never seriously threatened again after Folk's miss.

5. Key relief appearance from Winston fueled Giants

The Giants continued to win ugly Sunday , and they needed help from their benched quarterback to get it done. Jameis Winston lost his starting job to J.J. McCarthy, but when McCarthy got hurt against the Eagles, in came Winston for a crucial, go-ahead touchdown drive in the third quarter.

To that point, the Giants had kicked only field goals and trailed, 8-6. Early in the third quarter, McCarthy took a hit from the Eagles' Zack Baun and left with a hip injury. Winston took over and completed 6-of-8 passes for 71 yards, including a 5-yard TD throw to Isaiah Likely. Winston also converted a fourth-and-1 with a sneak.

That put the Giants up, 13-8. The Eagles never got the lead back. McCarthy eventually made it back in, and the Giants hung on for a 19-11 win. There's no controversy over who's starting Thursday against the Commanders, but the Giants might not have won this one without Winston's terrific drive.

articles.title: CeeDee Lamb is more than just a Dallas Cowboys superstar, and his latest off-field move makes that clear
articles.summary: CeeDee Lamb now has his own clothing line. The Dallas Cowboys wide receiver launched the 19-piece CeeDee Lamb Edit with Abercrombie & Fitch on Nov.
articles.body: CeeDee Lamb now has his own clothing line. The Dallas Cowboys wide receiver launched the 19-piece CeeDee Lamb Edit with Abercrombie & Fitch on Nov. 5, after traveling to the company’s headquarters in Columbus, Ohio, to work with its design team. Individual items are reported to cost between $40 and $260, and the collection is sold on the brand’s website and in select stores. Lamb has liked fashion for years, but this project let him decide how the clothes would look and feel instead of only wearing them in a shoot.CeeDee Lamb had a say in what went into the collectionAccording to a Nov. 4 press release from Abercrombie & Fitch, Lamb helped choose the colors, materials and designs alongside the brand’s designers. The pieces include jackets, sweaters, shirts, pants and even a necktie.It is dressier than his off-duty wardrobe, and the necktie is the clearest sign of that.The details are personal. One cardigan has his No. 88 on the buttons, and a pair of trousers carries the Roman numeral for 88 on the back pocket. There are no flashy jerseys or oversized logos. The numbers are easy to miss. A shopper who does not follow the Cowboys could wear the cardigan without it looking like team merchandise, while fans who know Lamb will spot the 88 right away.Lamb says his taste has changed as he has grown up. He wants classic pieces that last longer than one season, and the collection reflects that approach.Choosing materials is the less visible part of that job. Fabric decides how a sweater drapes and how a jacket holds up after a season of wear, and Lamb’s stated preference for pieces that last ties directly to those choices.The collection builds on Lamb’s earlier work with the brandLamb already had a history with Abercrombie & Fitch before this launch. He was part of its 2025 campaign, which arrived after the company became the official fashion partner of the NFL and the Cowboys.Back then he modeled the clothes. Now he helps shape what the brand sells, and most of it is everyday wear. For Abercrombie & Fitch, it gives the partnership a product to sell beyond ad images.The rollout was quick. The press release came out Nov. 4, and the collection launched a day later.Other athletes are taking similar steps. Serena Williams recently helped create a limited-edition Audemars Piguet watch. articles.title: John Harbaugh Addresses Jonathan Taylor Trade Rumors Involving Giants, Colts Ahead of NFL Deadline
articles.summary: New York Giants head coach John Harbaugh addressed a report from Sunday that the team pulled its offer for Indianapolis Colts running back Jonathan Taylor, and kept the door ajar for the team reopening those talks.
articles.body:
New York Giants head coach John Harbaugh addressed a report from Sunday that the team pulled its offer for Indianapolis Colts running back Jonathan Taylor, and kept the door ajar for the team reopening those talks.

"I'm not saying that report's not true. Those conversations are taking place," he told reporters following a 19-11 win over the Philadelphia Eagles. "If something happens for any player, can't talk about any [specific] player because they're with other teams right now, but we're not ruling anything out."

"I will say this: Things do change," he added. "Things change from day to day."

The Giants were reportedly offering Indy a second- and fifth-round pick for Taylor before removing themselves from talks.

And at this point, it seems like a guarantee that Taylor will be on the move before Tuesday's trade deadline:

Even if the Giants weren't dealing with injuries to Cam Skattebo (hamstring) missed and Tyrone Tracy Jr. (hamstring, injured reserve), Taylor would be a massive upgrade at running back for the team. The 27-year-old has rushed for 656 yards and eight touchdowns this season and rushed for more than 1,400 yards in both the 2024-25 campaigns.

New York moved to 5-2-1 on the season after beating the Birds on Sunday and are currently in the driver's seat to win the NFC East, with only the 4-5 Dallas Cowboys currently within striking distance. It makes sense that the team would consider some win-now moves, though mortgaging the future this early in the rebuild may be jumping the gun a bit. The Giants don't appear to be true Super Bowl contenders just yet.

In other words, while the Giants may not be completely out on Taylor, trading for him feels unlikely—and perhaps illogical, depending on the price tag—at this point.

articles.title: Jonathan Taylor delivers what sounds like a goodbye to Indianapolis after Colts' fifth straight loss

articles.title: Bryce Young, Sean Payton Discuss Broncos' End-Zone INT, Challenge vs. Panthers
articles.summary: A controversial moment came in the third quarter of Sunday's matchup between the Denver Broncos and the Carolina Panthers when Broncos head coach Sean Payton was granted a challenge after throwing his challenge flag at the last second.
articles.body:
A controversial moment came in the third quarter of Sunday's matchup between the Denver Broncos and the Carolina Panthers when Broncos head coach Sean Payton was granted a challenge after throwing his challenge flag at the last second.

Bryce Young's throw toward the end zone appeared to be intercepted after being tipped, but it was initially ruled incomplete. The Panthers then attempted to get their next play off, but Payton was granted a challenge.

Payton broke down the play from his point of view afterwards.

"So it comes kind of late, and I just gave [director of game management/assistant quarterbacks] Evan [Rothstein] a game ball," Payton told reporters . "That was a hard one for any one of us to see, and my concern was: Was anyone able to see that I threw it before the play was snapped? And fortunately, New York can."

Young, meanwhile, said his team should "never be relying on the refs."

Panthers head coach Dave Canales said after the game that the referees confirmed to him that Payton did throw the challenge flag before the snap.

"I gotta go from their word," Canales said. "You know, I don't have that at my disposal, but they did confirm that he got the flag off."

Had Payton not been granted the challenge, Sunday's game could have gone much differently.

The Panthers would have had the ball at Denver's 1-yardline while leading 14-13. They likely could have punched the ball in or at least gotten a field goal to extend the lead, but instead lost the ball in a crucial moment.

The Broncos then marched down the field and scored to take a 19-14 lead early in the fourth quarter. A Panthers three-and-out on the following drive set up another score for Denver to make it a 26-14 game.

The Panthers scored on the following drive to get a bit closer, but fumbled on their final offensive drive and allowed Denver to run the clock down.

The Broncos improved to 7-2 with the win, while Carolina fell to 3-5 and lost sole possession of first place in the NFC South.

While Young said the Panthers shouldn't have to rely on the refs to win games, the last-second challenge flag will certainly be on the minds of Carolina fans over the next few days.

articles.title: Caleb Williams, Bears Top Bucs Despite 5 Turnovers, Box Score Stats, Highlights for Mayfield, More
articles.summary: A wild Sunday Night Football matchup featuring seven total turnovers ended with Caleb Williams and the Chicago Bears securing a 27-24 win over Baker Mayfield and the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on a game-winning field goal at Soldier Field.
articles.body:
A wild Sunday Night Football matchup featuring seven total turnovers ended with Caleb Williams and the Chicago Bears securing a 27-24 win over Baker Mayfield and the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on a game-winning field goal at Soldier Field.

The Bears entered Sunday's home matchup as 6.5-point favorites over the Buccaneers, according to FanDuel Sportsbook , but did everything they could to give the game away as Williams threw four interceptions and the Bears tallied five turnovers.

Chicago has won four straight games, improving to 7-2 and moving into second place in the competitive NFC North where the Minnesota Vikings sit at top at 6-1.

Meanwhile, Tampa Bay fell to 3-6, dropping from first to third in the NFC South, where all four teams have losing records.

The Bears came out firing in the first quarter, with Rome Odunze hauling in his first touchdown of the year and Williams connecting with Luther Burden III for a 56-yard score to give Chicago a 14-0 lead.

That early cushion proved crucial as Williams threw three interceptions in the second quarter, limiting the Bears to just a field goal.

Mayfield threw an interception of his own, but Tampa Bay added two field goals in the quarter to cut the deficit to 17-6 at the half.

The interceptions continued to roll after halftime.

After the Buccaneers opened the second half with a Bucky Irving rushing touchdown, Williams and Mayfield traded interceptions on back-to-back possessions. However, Mayfield's proved costly as Jaylon Johnson returned it 67 yards for a pick-six.

Chicago carried a 24-13 lead into the fourth quarter Sunday night.

The Buccaneers opened the fourth quarter with a field goal to cut the deficit to one score.

Burden III then fumbled the ball, and Buccaneers safety Ifeatu Melifonwu recovered it, returning it to Chicago's 17-yard line. The turnover set up a two-play scoring drive capped by Irving's second rushing touchdown of the day, tying the game at 24 with a successful two-point conversion pass from Mayfield.

The Bears responded by running nearly three minutes off the clock before sealing the win with a 38-yard field goal.

Both Chicago and Tampa Bay head into its bye week.

articles.title: Caleb Williams Drops Bold Quote on Video After Throwing 4 INTs in Bears' Dramatic Win vs. Bucs
articles.summary: Chicago Bears quarterback Caleb Williams didn't exactly have a signature performance during his team's 27-24 win over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Sunday night, throwing four interceptions.
articles.body:
Chicago Bears quarterback Caleb Williams didn't exactly have a signature performance during his team's 27-24 win over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Sunday night, throwing four interceptions.

But don't expect him to suddenly become timid when he drops back to pass.

"I'm going to throw until I can't throw anymore," he told reporters following the victory. "That's how I live. I work my tail off to be in this position. I'll never not throw the ball. I could throw 100 picks in one game, if it comes down to it, I'm gonna throw that one pass I threw to Colston [Loveland]. Or if it's a tighter window I'm gonna rip it in there. That's how I grew up, that's what I am. I don't get gun shy. That's not me, that's not my identity, that's not who I am. With that, I'm gonna keep ripping it. Coach calls it, it's time to go make a play. Go through my reads, if it's not there check it down. If the shot's there, take it."

Williams did throw for 279 yards and two scores, so it wasn't all bad. But Chicago's five turnovers turned a game that looked like it might be a blowout after the Bears took a 14-0 lead in the first quarter into one that required a last-second field goal just to avoid overtime.

Tampa Bay's two turnovers and a few overly cautious decisions to kick field goals rather than take chances to get touchdowns also contributed to Chicago's eventual win.

While Williams isn't unlikely to grow more cautious, he also acknowledged that he could have played better and didn't pick up his teammates on Sunday night.

"Just try to be the big eraser. That's what I've been. That's what I will be," he told reporters . "I got to keep doing that, keep being the big eraser, and today I wasn't."

It wasn't exactly a feel-good win, in other words. But it was a win.

"They know that we didn't play as well as we're capable of playing," head coach Ben Johnson told reporters after the loss. "But I believe the best is yet to come in terms of our football in the back half of this season."

articles.title: Bears overcome 5 turnovers to beat Buccaneers 27-24 on ‘Sunday Night Football’
articles.summary: Caleb Williams found a wide-open Colston Loveland for a 38-yard catch to set up Cairo Santos’ 38-yard field goal as time expired, and the Chicago Bears picked up a sloppy 27-24 victory over Baker Mayfield and the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Sunday night.
articles.body: Caleb Williams found a wide-open Colston Loveland for a 38-yard catch to set up Cairo Santos’ 38-yard field goal as time expired, and the Chicago Bears picked up a sloppy 27-24 victory over Baker Mayfield and the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Sunday night. Chicago (7-2) committed five turnovers, including a career-high four interceptions by Williams. But he delivered after Mayfield rallied the Buccaneers in the final minutes. Loveland was pushed out of bounds at the Tampa Bay 16 with 40 seconds left. After two kneel-downs by Williams, Santos delighted the crowd of 60,470 by drilling his second field goal of the night. Chicago had a 24-16 lead when Luther Burden fumbled with 3:38 left and Tampa defensive back Ifeatu Melifonwu returned the ball to the Bears 17. Bucky Irving had an 11-yard carry before going in from the 6 for his second touchdown of the game. Mayfield scrambled for the 2-point conversion, tying it at 24 with 2:51 left. Mayfield was 18 for 32 for 243 yards and two interceptions. Irving finished with 97 yards on 20 carries. Mayfield failed to complete a pass in Tampa Bay’s previous game, a 16-0 win over Atlanta in wet conditions. The Buccaneers (3-6) rushed for a franchise-record 324 yards in the victory over the Falcons, including 170 by Irving. Williams was 22 for 37 for 279 yards and two touchdowns in Chicago’s fourth straight win. Burden had seven catches for 97 yards before he was shelved by a concussion. Jeffery Simmons had a sack in his first home game since he was acquired in a trade with Tennessee. The Buccaneers and Bears were the NFL’s top rushing teams going into the weekend, but there wasn’t much room to maneuver on the ground. The Bucs finished with 126 yards rushing, and the Bears had 72. Chicago had a 17-13 lead when Williams threw his fourth interception of the night, a deflected ball that landed in the hands of Tampa Bay linebacker Alex Anzalone. The Buccaneers took over at the Bears 37 with 4:32 left in the third quarter. One play later, Mayfield tried to throw the ball to Cade Otton, but Jaylon Johnson stepped in front of the tight end and returned the interception 67 yards for his second career pick-6. It was his first interception of the season. Chicago got off to a fast start, scoring on its first two possessions. Williams passed to a wide-open Rome Odunze for a 9-yard touchdown on the first drive of the game. Then Burden broke a couple of tackles while turning a third-and-8 reception into a 56-yard TD, making it 14-0 with 6:00 left in the first quarter. But the next two possessions for the Bears ended with interceptions by Williams, and the Buccaneers rallied by scoring on each side of halftime. Chase McLaughlin kicked a 21-yard field goal on the final play of the first half, and Tez Johnson’s 58-yard catch set up Irving’s 2-yard TD early in the third.

articles.title: Everything Baker Mayfield Said After Throwing 2 INTs in Bucs' Loss to Caleb Williams, Bears
articles.summary: The Tampa Bay Buccaneers lost an ugly, turnover-filled game to the Chicago Bears to drop to 3-6 on the season on Sunday.
articles.body:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers lost an ugly, turnover-filled game to the Chicago Bears to drop to 3-6 on the season on Sunday.

It was an upgrade from last week in some ways for Baker Mayfield after completing no passes against the Atlanta Falcons, but the Bucs' quarterback still had a day to forget.

Mayfield threw for 243 yards and two interceptions on 18-of-32 passing. He was sacked four times and had a passer rating of 54.6 in the 27-24 loss.

"It sucks, but the team fought," Mayfield told reporters. "Team fought and stayed in it. That's one of the top teams, if not the top team in the league right there, so if we play clean football, we'd be proud of that."

While Mayfield committed fewer turnovers than Bears quarterback Caleb Williams, who threw four interceptions, he had the most costly pick of the game.

The Bucs trailed 17-13 in the third quarter and had the ball in Chicago territory following an interception, but on the second play of the drive, Mayfield tried to find Cade Otton but instead threw the ball into the hands of Jaylon Johnson, who took it into the end zone for a pick-six.

"Don't want to have them ever, but especially when it turns into immediate points on the pick-six," Mayfield said. "That obviously was the difference in the game."

Tampa Bay eventually tied things up after a field goal and a touchdown followed by a two-point conversion from Mayfield, but Chicago ultimately won it on a walk-off field goal.

It's been a rough season for Mayfield, who has battled injuries and now has more interceptions (4) than touchdowns (3), but playing in a weak NFC South means the Bucs' playoff hopes are still alive.

Mayfield will look to flush the rough showing and turn things around heading into the second half of the season.

"Need to get it fixed," Mayfield said. "Gotta take this bye to get healthy, continue to get guys back, and just have it in our minds that we need to go on a run. Mentally, it needs to be that way."

articles.title: Patrick Mahomes proves he is indestructible while Joe Burrow, Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins light up Madrid - NFL Sunday Review
articles.summary: NFL Sunday Review - we reflect on Week Nine in the NFL as the Cincinnati Bengals stars dazzled in Madrid, Patrick Mahomes overcame an injury scare and Myles Garrett made an emphatic return from injury in his first big day for the Los Angeles Rams
articles.body:
Thousands of Spanish fans will have left the Bernabeu on Sunday with either a strengthened or a new-found connection to the Bengals, who delivered about as good a product as you are likely to see in an international game as they beat the Atlanta Falcons 34-17 on the league's return to Madrid.

A winning product. A Super Bowl-contending product. The product of a three-headed monster capable of taking a sledgehammer to any defense in football, and one built to thrive amid the fiercest of slugfests.

Find yourself in a shoot-out with these Bengals and you are likely to come out second best. Particularly against this version of Burrow.

There is a growing argument this version is flirting with the best version of Burrow in his NFL career as he seeks to fulfil his own rallying cry for Championship urgency this past offseason.

He was insistent "this is it" as far as Cincinnati's Super Bowl quest was concerned, long-tired of slow starts and injury setbacks that have hindered their mission to get back to the 'Big Dance', where they fell short against the Los Angeles Rams four years ago.

Burrow was near-flawless on European soil as he threw for 271 yards and three touchdowns while rushing for another himself, which he capped by imitating a Neymar celebration. Whether the Brazilian icon played for Real or not, the locals enjoyed it, so too his admiration for the city's museum scene this week.

"I always whisper in his ear to be legendary. That's who he is and that's what he does," Bengals defensive tackle Dexter Lawrence told Sky Sports NFL .

"He's the greatest. We keep calling him a killer - he goes out there with that look in his eye and does what he's supposed to do and puts point on the board."

Head coach Zac Taylor admitted after the game the difficulty in resisting temptation to make every play a passing play such has been Burrow's dominance this season. As much was evident in his reply to Atlanta's opening touchdown when he launched deep to Chase for the 47-yard touchdown that would open the floodgates for Cincinnati's command.

"When I saw that first touchdown I was like 'uh oh', it was a snowball effect," said Higgins after the game.

It represented their 19th touchdown connection of at least 40 yards to tie Joe Montana and Jerry Rice for the third-most by a quarterback-receiver duo since 1980, behind only Peyton Manning and Marvin Harrison (21) and Steve Young and Rice (20).

It is unfair. It is rude. It should be illegal to have a Chase-Higgins pairing at the disposal of a full-flow Burrow; together they are borderline unstoppable. There was a moment during Higgins' second touchdown of the game when both myself and a colleague pointed towards Chase, who had also wriggled free in the end zone to give Burrow a dream pick-your-poison scenario.

There are defensive coordinators across the NFL that might relate to Higgins' 'uh oh' sentiment upon a Burrow-Chase union. It tends to spell trouble, and there tends to be zero remedies.

The celebration of choice on Chase's touchdown was a matador display as Higgins played the role of charging bull, much to the delight of the Bernabeu crowd. The game's chief protagonists were winning both on the football field but also in the realm of international fandom.

"The fans liked it, 'we did it and I heard them say 'Oleeee'," Higgins said.

There are plenty more 'Oles' to follow this season for an offensive trio playing at a different level to most in the league right now. Discussion surrounding the Bengals' Super Bowl aspirations has usually come back to question marks over their defense, which is why their offseason trade for Dexter Lawrence felt like a potential needle-moving moment.

The reality, though, is that defensive improvement never really needed to be needle-moving or transformative, but instead a meaningful step forward. That is courtesy of a luxury to which few can attest in a trio of Burrow, Chase and Higgins.

Higgins is automatic with one of the safest pairs of suction hands in football and the catch radius to defy any angle or the tightest of man coverage. Chase is a demon with the ball in his hands and a single high safeties worst nightmare come true. So long as that three-headed monster remains intact, the Bengals can challenge for the Super Bowl.

Patrick Mahomes is seemingly indestructible. Robert Saleh - the now Tennessee Titans head coach - once said of the Kansas City Chiefs QB: "Don't be fooled by his little old man jog".

The three-time Super Bowl winner played through a high ankle sprain in leading KC back from a double-digit deficit to beat the Philadelphia Eagles to one of those titles, while he also overcame turf toe to reach another Super Bowl (which they would lose to Tom Brady's Tampa Bay Buccaneers).

When it looks like this man might be done, he is not. And that was very much the case again on Sunday when Mahomes' throwing arm appeared to be badly injured on a strip-sack by the New York Jets' David Bailey just before half-time - the Chiefs only leading 14-12 at the time.

There were some hugely concerned faces on the sideline, none more so than the man himself, as well as tight end buddy Travis Kelce. But, incredibly, after a bit of treatment, No 15 was ready to go again, leading his team on a second-half tear to secure a comfortable 23-point victory in the end.

The New York Giants are seemingly eyeing a trade for Indianapolis Colts running back Jonathan Taylor, with Big Blue head coach John Harbaugh saying "those conversations are taking place".

Fox Sports reported on Sunday morning that the Giants had already offered the Colts second and fifth-round draft picks for Taylor, which has not yet got the deal done.

But the Giants, currently in the driver's seat in the NFC East, are keen to get a deal done with Cam Skattebo (hamstring) missing Sunday's win over the Philadelphia Eagles, Tyrone Tracy Jr (hamstring) on injured reserve and Devin Singletary returning only 31 yards on 21 carries in Philly.

Taylor, meanwhile, acknowledged he might have played his last game in Indy. "This place helped shape me into the man I am today, so I'm very grateful," Taylor said after their home loss to the Dallas Cowboys. "If it is [my last game], I'm very grateful for the city of Indianapolis."

The trade deadline is on Tuesday November 10.

The Bengals do not need to trade for Jonathan Taylor. 'Need' is a strong word, and there are two sides to the equation when it comes to a potential move for a star running back. Cincinnati want the ball in the hands of their quarterback as much as humanly possible - would it be right and would it be wise to add a centre-piece running back to a scheme that is not only built but functions on shot-gun aerial bombardment?

The other side is the Thanos 'final Infinity Stone' notion to pairing Taylor with Burrow, Chase and Higgins, which becomes every bit the Avengers of NFL offenses and the kind capable of steamrolling its way to a Super Bowl appearance. Taylor is a field-flipper and an immediate difference-maker - but how different do you really want this offense to look?

Chase Brown barely gets a sniff in comparison to other backs around the league; when the Bengals did call on his number in Madrid he helped pave the way for Higgins' second touchdown catch. Sure, it would be box office. But to say the Bengals need him would be a disservice to just how good their prized trio are.

Myles Garrett: A warm welcome back to the Rams for Mr Myles Garrett. Los Angeles' 20-13 road win over the Washington Commanders has them over .500 for the first time in a season which they were expected to dominate - in large part due to their blockbuster offseason addition of the two-time NFL Defensive Player of the Year, who has been missing due to injury since their season opener.

But he is back, and with a vengeance, as he returned three sacks against the Commanders, the first of which being a forced fumble. Finally paired with three-time DPOY Aaron Donald on the defensive line, the Rams having won three straight, maybe a Super Bowl run could still be on the cards?

Christian Watson and Matthew Golden: The Green Bay Packers are explosive on offense! And the great beneficiaries of Jordan Love continuing to air it out - and coach Matt LaFleur laying the table for him to do so - are receivers Christian Watson and Matthew Golden.

Watson came down with 171 yards and a score off seven catches, while Golden 164 off 10 grabs and too found the end zone - career highs for both - as Green Bay put up 45 points on a Pats defense that practically carried them through the playoffs and to the Super Bowl last season. Don't sleep on the Packers.

The Chargers gonna keep Chargering. If you thought it could not get any worse for head coach Jim Harbaugh, OC Mike McDaniel, QB Justin Herbert and the still-winless Chargers, you would be wrong!

This Los Angeles offense stinks! Do not let a couple of fourth-quarter, garbage-time touchdowns fool you. The Chargers were trailing 38-9 prior, notching three field goals to go with four punts, an interception, turnover on downs and fumble from their other offensive series.

They are now 0-8 on a truly dismal season.

Dan Quinn: In a Washington Commanders season defined by late offensive blunders or clock mismanagement, their head coach might well have dropped the ball once more to potentially signal curtains for him in the country's capital.

Down seven, on the final play of their loss to the Los Angeles Rams - set up just beyond their opponents' 30-yard line - the Commanders opted to go for a short pass followed by a couple of lame attempts at laterals, rather than take a shot at the end zone.

After the game, Quinn admitted he was "not happy with the execution of that play".

Well, file it alongside Jayden Daniels' sack in the dying seconds of overtime as their Week Five game against the New York Giants ended in a tie, as well as Quinn seeming to forget what down it was a week later in the loss to the San Francisco 49ers.

Player of the Weekend - Arvell Reese, LB, New York Giants

The Philadelphia Eagles are there to be preyed on at the moment, and the New York Giants willingly obliged. Linebacker Arvell Reese in particular feasted to bolster his Defensive Rookie of the Year campaign, logging three sacks, 12 tackles, three tackles for loss, a forced fumble, four pressures and three quarterback hits to torment Eagles back-up quarterback Joe Milton in a 19-11 victory. His 2.29 seconds to sack marked the fastest time in the NFL this season, according to Next Gen Stats. The Giants have a superstar stalwart on their hands.

Sean Payton's Denver Broncos only know how to win close games. In fact, Sunday's 26-21 victory over the Carolina Panthers means they have now won 16 straight one-score games.

The Broncos survived late when Nik Bonitto strip-sacked Bryce Young and recovered the loose fumble with 1.24 remaining, before Bo Nix clinched the win with a quarterback sneak on third down.

It was what has become typical late Broncos drama. Denver had trailed by one point entering the fourth quarter, meaning it would become their fifth victory of the year after trailing in the fourth. For a large part of the game Young had been sizzling, only to be hit by Broncos defiance.

articles.title: NFL results: Chicago Bears and Denver Broncos grind out wins in week nine
articles.summary: The Chicago Bears and Denver Broncos grind out wins while the Cincinnati Bengals and Green Bay Packers put on a show as the NFL season reaches the halfway point.
articles.body:
The potential Super Bowl contenders are starting to emerge in the NFL with the regular season having reached its halfway point this weekend.

The San Francisco 49ers have the league's best record after winning on Sunday and will be joined on 7-1 by either the Buffalo Bills or Minnesota Vikings - provided they do not have a tie in Monday's game.

The Chicago Bears and Denver Broncos both ground out hard-fought wins to improve to 7-2 heading into their bye weeks.

The Cincinnati Bengals put on a show as the NFL's international series continued while the Green Bay Packers outclassed one of last season's Super Bowl teams.

Here are the top stories from week nine in the NFL.

After winning at defending champions Seattle last week, Chicago looked set for another impressive victory as they charged into a 14-0 lead against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in Sunday's primetime game.

Bears quarterback Caleb Williams then threw a career-high four interceptions before the Bucs drew level with three minutes remaining.

But Williams managed to lead the hosts into field-goal range, with Cairo Santos making a 38-yard kick as time expired to beat the Bucs 27-24 for Chicago's fourth straight win.

The Bears are now second in the NFC North, the only division in which all four teams have a winning record, but will go top if the Vikings lose to the Bills on Monday.

Denver are top of the AFC West after they scored two touchdowns in the final quarter and sacked Carolina Panthers quarterback Bryce Young with just over a minute left to clinch a 26-21 road win.

Not only did it extend the Broncos' winning run to five but was their 16th straight win in one-score games in the regular season - a new NFL record.

Joe Burrow attended Milan fashion week this summer and modelled in Paris in 2024, but this week he visited Madrid to play his first international game.

The Cincinnati Bengals quarterback vowed to put on a show at the Bernabeu Stadium in the seventh of a record nine international games this season, and the Bengals did just that as they beat the Atlanta Falcons 34-17 to go 6-2.

After being involved in six touchdowns last week, Burrow played a part in another four in Spain. The 29-year-old completed 24 of his 29 passes for 271 yards to cement himself as a contender for his first Most Valuable Player award.

Ja'Marr Chase had a season-high 155 receiving yards as the Bengals scored more than 30 points for a fourth straight game – tying a team record.

The Bengals are now 6-2 and joint-top of the AFC North with the Pittsburgh Steelers, who they face in next Sunday's primetime game.

Their divisional rivals the Cleveland Browns lost 23-22 at the New Orleans Saints in overtime.

Four-time Super Bowl winner Rob Gronkowski was inducted into the New England Patriots' hall of fame while his former team-mate Tom Brady returned to Gillette Stadium for the first time in his broadcasting career.

Yet they had to watch Green Bay quarterback Jordan Love put on a masterclass as the Packers romped to a 45-27 win against a New England team that reached last season's Super Bowl. It was the most points the Patriots had allowed at home since 1970.

Love went deep time and again, racking up 372 passing yards, three touchdown passes and a touchdown run. Wide receivers Christian Watson and Matthew Golden became the first Green Bay players to each claim more than 150 receiving yards and a touchdown in the same game since 1942.

Brady and Gronkowski are third all-time for passing yards from a quarterback-tight end duo (9,186) and Kansas City Chiefs pair Patrick Mahomes and Travis Kelce went top of that list on Sunday.

Mahomes brushed off an injury scare against the New York Jets to ensure he and Kelce surpassed Philip Rivers and Antonio Gates (9,352) to reach 9,360 during a 35-12 win for the Chiefs.

Myles Garrett and Aaron Donald finally played together for the first time as the Los Angeles Rams won 20-13 at the Washington Commanders.

After making his Rams debut in Australia in week one, Garrett needed knee surgery and Donald didn't make his return from retirement until week two.

While Donald, 35, is still waiting for his first sack of the season, Garrett claimed three and forced a fumble to help the former Super Bowl favourites clinch a third straight win.

Puka Nacua racked up 150 receiving yards and a touchdown but could join fellow wide receiver Davante Adams (hamstring) on the sidelines as he injured a knee. Nacua will have an MRI on Monday.

Although the Rams are now 5-4, their NFC West rivals the San Francisco 49ers and Seattle Seahawks both got back to winning ways.

The 49ers (7-1) won 38-17 against the Las Vegas Raiders while defending champions Seattle (5-4) beat the Arizona Cardinals 17-3.

The Indianapolis Colts have already begun a rebuild, trading away two key players during the season, and they could have more big-name departures before the trade deadline on Tuesday.

The Colts slipped to 2-7 with a 27-23 loss to the Dallas Cowboys but had already been in talks over running back Jonathan Taylor, their prized asset.

They have reportedly taken calls about quarterback Daniel Jones too, while wide receiver Josh Downs has requested a trade.

The New York Giants withdrew an offer for Taylor but head coach John Harbaugh said that "things do change" after Sunday's 19-11 win over the Philadelphia Eagles – a seventh straight loss for Philly and the Giants' first win at their divisional rivals in 13 years.

Down to their third-choice quarterback, the Baltimore Ravens have completed a trade for Jacoby Brissett from Arizona but despite speculation over Derrick Henry, the Ravens reportedly have no intention of trading the veteran running back.

Arizona pair Budda Baker and Josh Sweat have been linked with a trade while there has been interest in wide receiver Brian Thomas Jr, who has slipped down the pecking order at the 6-2 Jacksonville Jaguars.

articles.title: Bears overcome Caleb Williams' career-high 4 interceptions, but Bucs give Ben Johnson's team, QB heat check
articles.summary: Chicago completed its primetime sweep, winning its third night game in a row, except its five-turnover performance may slow the roll on all the Super Bowl ta...
articles.body:
CHICAGO — Caleb Williams was having his way until he got in his own way Sunday night at Soldier Field. In his words, the Bears quarterback "got greedy," forcing the issue in the red zone, resulting in his first second-quarter interception against the Buccaneers.

So was the whole night, really — not only for Williams, who wound up throwing a career-high four picks after entering with a 0.6% interception rate, but also for a Chicago team that was on top of the football world in the wake of its statement-making Monday night victory over the Seattle Seahawks.

Williams went from toying with the Buccaneers' defense to floundering against its unrelenting pressure. The Bears committed five turnovers and were responsible for a collection of special teams mishaps.

"And, yet, we still found a way," second-year head coach Ben Johnson said at the podium in the aftermath of a 27-24 win that bumped Chicago to 7-2.

A Bears defense that continues to evolve in the presence of recently acquired defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons picked up the slack. Plus, when it mattered most — with the game tied 24-24 and less than three minutes remaining — Williams delivered. He capitalized on Tampa Bay's blown coverage, connecting with tight end Colston Loveland for a 38-yard gain that set the stage for a game-winning 38-yard Cairo Santos field goal .

"I'm gonna throw until I can't throw anymore," Williams said postgame. "That's how I live. I work my tail off to be in this position. I'll never not throw the ball.

"I could throw 100 picks in one game. If it comes down to it, I'm going to throw that pass that I threw to Colston, or if it's a tighter window, I'm going to rip it in there."

Williams, who piled up 279 yards on 22-of-37 passing — to go along with two touchdowns and his bounty of picks — emphasized that he doesn't get gun-shy.

He called back to a three-interception game he had in high school. He also logged three picks versus Notre Dame amid his final go-around at USC.

"The other two times, we didn't win the games," the 24-year-old Williams noted. "This time, it's a 'W.' So, uncharted territory in that sense."

Williams is used to being an eraser: 'Today I wasn't'

Early in Sunday night's game, Williams' only kryptonite was himself.

A week removed from authoring a 17-play, 80-yard touchdown drive on their first possession versus the Seahawks, the Bears' opening script resulted in another TD. Williams picked up where he left off, continuing his heater by flashing his ability to fire from any arm slot on a 13-yard rip to rookie wideout Zavion Thomas. He capped the 10-play series by throwing on the run, as he did repeatedly against a characteristically blitz-happy Todd Bowles defense. Williams hooked up with a sliding Rome Odunze, as the wideout made a redemptive scoring grab after bobbling himself out of one moments prior.

On the next drive, Williams gave Luther Burden III a runner's ball. The speedy receiver hauled it on his slant and teleported in space, breaking a pair of Buccaneers tackles during his 56-yard catch-and-run touchdown that put Chicago up 14-0 with six minutes left in the opening frame.

Williams was escaping from the duress Tampa Bay was creating, slicing its blitz calls with precision passing, going 6 of 8 for 105 yards and two TDs over those first two drives. His two incompletions in that stretch were the byproduct of drops.

Then, what began as arguably his best series yet ended with the first of his several mistakes. After Williams converted his signature jump pass — perhaps a foreboding one in hindsight — and connected with Odunze once more, that time on a fadeaway, he drove the ball into coverage. That ill-advised pass followed a Thomas unnecessary roughness penalty on first-and-goal that backed the Bears up.

Williams was aiming for Odunze again, except Tampa Bay standout cornerback Jacob Parrish was there, and soon safety Tykee Smith was, too. Smith swooped in for the pick.

One snap after Tampa Bay quarterback Baker Mayfield was denied a chains-moving sneak on fourth-and-1 from the Buccaneers' 35-yard line midway through the second quarter, Williams unleashed a pass while retreating and just before he was hit. The ball hung in the air for what felt like a minute. Tampa Bay cornerback Zyon McCollum came down with it, toe-tapping to secure the first of his two interceptions.

"Just tried to get the ball out and tried to be the big eraser," Williams said of that giveaway. "That's what I've been. That's what I will be. Yeah, keep doing that, keep being the big eraser, and today I wasn't."

That means covering up flubs, whether that be by throwing the ball out of bounds or making something out of nothing with his Houdini-like scramble ability.

Doing so calls for walking a fine line. The 2024 No. 1 overall draft pick usually does.

McCollum picked him off again late in the second quarter, immediately after Bears safety Cam Lewis intercepted Mayfield in a game that featured a total of six INTs and seven turnovers.

With pressure in his face, Williams dialed up one of his jump passes. It fluttered well beyond wideout Kalif Raymond and was ultimately cradled by a diving McCollum.

Tampa Bay went on to kick a field goal to make it a 17-6 game at half, after which a 58-yard Mayfield-to-Tez Johnson completion paved the way for a 2-yard rushing touchdown from running back Bucky Irving.

Fortunately for Williams, his fourth pick — the least egregious of the bunch, given that it stemmed from a deflection — was erased by someone else.

Cornerback Jaylon Johnson, a two-time Pro Bowler who had a rough 2026 campaign so far, stepped in front of a Mayfield pass and ran it back for a 67-yard pick-6, in part thanks to a block from defensive end Montez Sweat that sent Mayfield pinwheeling.

"I remember we all sat on the bench. We were on the sideline," Raymond explained in the locker room, when asked about Johnson's defensive TD. "We were like, 'I don't think there's anybody we could be happier for to go out there and do that,' because of how much time he has spent the last eight weeks after practice catching footballs, catching those picks. I mean, he's one of the last guys out there getting stuff done on defense."

Mayfield, still not 100 percent after returning midseason from a thumb injury on his throwing hand, finished 18-of-32 passing with 243 yards. Having completed a combined seven passes over the two previous games, he upped the ante in Chicago and nearly helped his 3-6 Bucs pull off a stunning comeback.

Burden suffered a seismic blow from Tampa Bay edge rusher Rueben Bain Jr., fumbling the ball and now dealing with what Ben Johnson described as a concussion.

That final Bears turnover presented the Buccaneers a short field. Irving scampered in for his second TD to knot things up.

Williams and Loveland, as well as Santos, prevented overtime and furthered the Bears' four-game win streak. It's worth noting that Chicago was facing a Tampa Bay defense that came in ranking first in the NFL in takeaways and EPA per play allowed. Even so, as Loveland said at his locker, it was a "bad display of football."

Offensively, he meant. Special teams weren't much better, however.

"They know that we didn't play as well as we're capable of playing," Johnson said. "But I believe the best is yet to come, in terms of our football in the back half of this season."

On Sunday, the Bears still tied off their prime-time sweep, an early holiday gift to a fan base starving for the franchise's first Lombardi Trophy since it won one during its fabled 1985 season under the late Mike Ditka.

Chicago has won three straight standalone night games, the first two of which saw Johnson's group take down the teams that played in last season's Super Bowl. The Bears held off the New England Patriots on "Thursday Night Football" and then beat the defending champion Seahawks on "Monday Night Football."

They weren't the same marvel on "Sunday Night Football." But they didn't have to be, and maybe that justifies their status as a title contender.

"We obviously want to be clicking on all three, but when a side of the ball isn't clicking, we're going to step up, we're going to stand up for each other," Williams said. "Defense did that today."
